For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. PFI2-026 针叶木8000转那组的干纸抗张指数，每次平行实验的原始数据能给我列一下吗？

两版保留没有逐次重复数字、未看图不报读数及测试标准；新版明显缩短。文中未说明图的误差棒定义与图本身有没有误差棒要区分。

固定初稿
**结论：该文献没有给出“针叶木 8000 转”组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据。**

具体情况（Li 等, 2020, PFI 打浆/纤维素聚集结构研究）：

- 打浆条件：商品漂白针叶木硫酸盐浆经 PFI 打浆，转数 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 转；针叶木 8000 转对应约 40 °SR[3]。
- 干纸抗张强度的测试方法仅说明按 TAPPI T494 执行，未给出试样数量、平行次数或单次测量值[6]。
- 抗张指数结果**仅以图的形式**呈现：抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度均作为打浆转数的函数画在 Figure 3 中（针叶木为 a 图、阔叶木为 b 图）[11][20]。正文只讨论“随打浆转数上升、源于细纤维化和细组分增加”的趋势，没有列出任何数值表格[20]。
- 文中唯一的数据表（Table 1、Table 2）分别是结晶度/晶粒尺寸和氢键相对含量，与力学性能无关[1][2]。

因此：

1. 无法列出“8000 转针叶木”干纸抗张指数的平行原始值——文献中不存在这类数据；
2. 若需要该点数值，只能从 Figure 3(a) 读图获得近似值（可能带误差棒，但误差棒含义/重复次数文中未交代）；我尚未查看该图的具体像素，因此不给出读数以免臆测；
3. 建议查找该文补充材料（Supplementary，仅含 XRD 拟合、FT-IR 拟合与 BET 数据[5]）或直接联系作者索取原始记录。

如果你手上另有一篇给出“平行实验表格”的文献（例如中文期刊的制浆造纸实验论文），可以告诉我题目或关键词，我再帮你定位具体数据表。
旧复核
**结论：该文献没有给出“针叶木 8000 转”组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据。**

具体情况（Li 等, 2020, PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构的影响）：

- 打浆条件：商品漂白针叶木与阔叶木硫酸盐浆经 PFI 打浆，转数均为 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 转；打浆浓度 10%，磨盘间隙 0.2 mm，针叶木与阔叶木单位齿长作用力分别为 3.33 N/mm 和 1.77 N/mm[3]。按文中给出的打浆度序列，针叶木依次为 16、20、40、63、79 °SR，即 8000 转组对应约 40 °SR（该序列首项原文标注为 16 °SR，与“0 转”并列，可视为未打浆组对应值）[3]。
- 干纸抗张强度测试方法仅说明按 TAPPI T494 执行（湿纸幅强度按 GB/T 12914-2008，零-span 按 ISO 15361），未给出试样数量、平行次数、标准差或单次测量值[6]。
- 抗张指数结果**仅以图的形式**呈现：抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度作为打浆转数的函数绘于 Figure 3（(a) 针叶木、(b) 阔叶木）[11][20]。正文只描述随打浆转数升高而增加的趋势，并把该增量主要归因于打浆过程中细纤维化与细组分（fines）的增加；这是作者的解释，文中未提供能把二者分离的因果证据[20]。
- 文中数据表（Table 1 结晶度与晶粒尺寸、Table 2 氢键相对含量）与力学性能无关[1][2]；正文提到细纤维化随打浆进行而增强，与比表面积增大（Online Resource 表 S1）一致[14]，但同样不涉及抗张指数的重复数据。

因此：

1. 无法列出“针叶木 8000 转”干纸抗张指数的逐次平行原始值——所查文献中不存在此类数据，也无法据此判断该组数值的高低排序或组间差异是否显著；
2. 若仅需该点的近似水平，只能从 Figure 3(a) 读图获得（是否带误差棒及误差棒所代表的重复次数文中未说明）；我尚未查看该图像素，故不给出具体读数；
3. 补充材料（Supplementary）仅含 XRD 拟合结果、FT-IR 拟合曲线、BET 等温线及孔结构表，不含力学原始数据[5]；如需逐次数据，建议直接联系作者索取原始记录，或查阅明确以表格形式报告平行实验的文献。

证据缺口：缺少“8000 转针叶木干纸抗张指数平均值±偏差/逐次值”及重复次数；该缺口在所查文献内无法解决。
新复核
**结论：该文献没有提供“针叶木 8000 转”这一组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据，因此无法列出。**

依据与说明：Li 等（2020）的 PFI 打浆研究中，

- 针叶木浆在转数为 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 的 PFI 下打浆；其中 8000 转时针叶木的 SR 值为 40°SR[3]。
- 干纸抗张强度只注明按 TAPPI T494 测试，并未交代试样数量、平行次数或单次测量值[6]。
- 抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度都只以“随打浆转数变化”的曲线形式出现在 Figure 3 中，针叶木为 (a) 图、阔叶木为 (b) 图[11][20]；正文只说明抗张强度随打浆转数升高而增大，并将其归因于打浆过程产生的细纤维化和细组分增加[20]。这是作者给出的解释，并未证明机制。
- 文中没有抗张指数的数值表；仅有 Table 1（结晶度、晶粒尺寸）和 Table 2（氢键相对含量），它们与力学性能无关[1][2]。
- 补充材料仅含 XRD 拟合、FT-IR 拟合与 BET 数据[5]，不包含力学平行数据。

+- 打浆条件：商品漂白针叶木与阔叶木硫酸盐浆经 PFI 打浆，转数均为 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 转；打浆浓度 10%，磨盘间隙 0.2 mm，针叶木与阔叶木单位齿长作用力分别为 3.33 N/mm 和 1.77 N/mm[3]。按文中给出的打浆度序列，针叶木依次为 16、20、40、63、79 °SR，即 8000 转组对应约 40 °SR（该序列首项原文标注为 16 °SR，与“0 转”并列，可视为未打浆组对应值）[3]。

+- 文中数据表（Table 1 结晶度与晶粒尺寸、Table 2 氢键相对含量）与力学性能无关[1][2]；正文提到细纤维化随打浆进行而增强，与比表面积增大（Online Resource 表 S1）一致[14]，但同样不涉及抗张指数的重复数据。

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. This made cellulose more accessible to water and chemicals. However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds.         "text": "**结论：该文献没有给出“针叶木 8000 转”组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据。**\n\n具体情况（Li 等, 2020, PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构的影响）：\n\n- 打浆条件：商品漂白针叶木与阔叶木硫酸盐浆经 PFI 打浆，转数均为 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 转；打浆浓度 10%，磨盘间隙 0.2 mm，针叶木与阔叶木单位齿长作用力分别为 3.33 N/mm 和 1.77 N/mm[3]。按文中给出的打浆度序列，针叶木依次为 16、20、40、63、79 °SR，即 8000 转组对应约 40 °SR（该序列首项原文标注为 16 °SR，与“0 转”并列，可视为未打浆组对应值）[3]。\n- 干纸抗张强度测试方法仅说明按 TAPPI T494 执行（湿纸幅强度按 GB/T 12914-2008，零-span 按 ISO 15361），未给出试样数量、平行次数、标准差或单次测量值[6]。\n- 抗张指数结果**仅以图的形式**呈现：抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度作为打浆转数的函数绘于 Figure 3（(a) 针叶木、(b) 阔叶木）[11][20]。正文只描述随打浆转数升高而增加的趋势，并把该增量主要归因于打浆过程中细纤维化与细组分（fines）的增加；这是作者的解释，文中未提供能把二者分离的因果证据[20]。\n- 文中数据表（Table 1 结晶度与晶粒尺寸、Table 2 氢键相对含量）与力学性能无关[1][2]；正文提到细纤维化随打浆进行而增强，与比表面积增大（Online Resource 表 S1）一致[14]，但同样不涉及抗张指数的重复数据。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "E14",
        "basis": {
          "type": "reference_evidence",
          "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."
        }

        "text": "**结论：该文献没有给出“针叶木 8000 转”组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据。**\n\n具体情况（Li 等, 2020, PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构的影响）：\n\n- 打浆条件：商品漂白针叶木与阔叶木硫酸盐浆经 PFI 打浆，转数均为 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 转；打浆浓度 10%，磨盘间隙 0.2 mm，针叶木与阔叶木单位齿长作用力分别为 3.33 N/mm 和 1.77 N/mm[3]。按文中给出的打浆度序列，针叶木依次为 16、20、40、63、79 °SR，即 8000 转组对应约 40 °SR（该序列首项原文标注为 16 °SR，与“0 转”并列，可视为未打浆组对应值）[3]。\n- 干纸抗张强度测试方法仅说明按 TAPPI T494 执行（湿纸幅强度按 GB/T 12914-2008，零-span 按 ISO 15361），未给出试样数量、平行次数、标准差或单次测量值[6]。\n- 抗张指数结果**仅以图的形式**呈现：抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度作为打浆转数的函数绘于 Figure 3（(a) 针叶木、(b) 阔叶木）[11][20]。正文只描述随打浆转数升高而增加的趋势，并把该增量主要归因于打浆过程中细纤维化与细组分（fines）的增加；这是作者的解释，文中未提供能把二者分离的因果证据[20]。\n- 文中数据表（Table 1 结晶度与晶粒尺寸、Table 2 氢键相对含量）与力学性能无关[1][2]；正文提到细纤维化随打浆进行而增强，与比表面积增大（Online Resource 表 S1）一致[14]，但同样不涉及抗张指数的重复数据。",

The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers.   "fixed_draft": "**结论：该文献没有给出“针叶木 8000 转”组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据。**\n\n具体情况（Li 等, 2020, PFI 打浆/纤维素聚集结构研究）：\n\n- 打浆条件：商品漂白针叶木硫酸盐浆经 PFI 打浆，转数 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 转；针叶木 8000 转对应约 40 °SR[3]。\n- 干纸抗张强度的测试方法仅说明按 TAPPI T494 执行，未给出试样数量、平行次数或单次测量值[6]。\n- 抗张指数结果**仅以图的形式**呈现：抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度均作为打浆转数的函数画在 Figure 3 中（针叶木为 a 图、阔叶木为 b 图）[11][20]。正文只讨论“随打浆转数上升、源于细纤维化和细组分增加”的趋势，没有列出任何数值表格[20]。\n- 文中唯一的数据表（Table 1、Table 2）分别是结晶度/晶粒尺寸和氢键相对含量，与力学性能无关[1][2]。\n\n因此：\n\n1. 无法列出“8000 转针叶木”干纸抗张指数的平行原始值——文献中不存在这类数据；\n2. 若需要该点数值，只能从 Figure 3(a) 读图获得近似值（可能带误差棒，但误差棒含义/重复次数文中未交代）；我尚未查看该图的具体像素，因此不给出读数以免臆测；\n3. 建议查找该文补充材料（Supplementary，仅含 XRD 拟合、FT-IR 拟合与 BET 数据[5]）或直接联系作者索取原始记录。\n\n如果你手上另有一篇给出“平行实验表格”的文献（例如中文期刊的制浆造纸实验论文），可以告诉我题目或关键词，我再帮你定位具体数据表。",

    "answer": "**结论：该文献没有提供“针叶木 8000 转”这一组干纸抗张指数的逐次平行实验原始数据，因此无法列出。**\n\n依据与说明：Li 等（2020）的 PFI 打浆研究中，\n\n- 针叶木浆在转数为 0、4000、8000、12 000、16 000 的 PFI 下打浆；其中 8000 转时针叶木的 SR 值为 40°SR[3]。\n- 干纸抗张强度只注明按 TAPPI T494 测试，并未交代试样数量、平行次数或单次测量值[6]。\n- 抗张指数、零-span 抗张指数和湿纸幅强度都只以“随打浆转数变化”的曲线形式出现在 Figure 3 中，针叶木为 (a) 图、阔叶木为 (b) 图[11][20]；正文只说明抗张强度随打浆转数升高而增大，并将其归因于打浆过程产生的细纤维化和细组分增加[20]。这是作者给出的解释，并未证明机制。\n- 文中没有抗张指数的数值表；仅有 Table 1（结晶度、晶粒尺寸）和 Table 2（氢键相对含量），它们与力学性能无关[1][2]。\n- 补充材料仅含 XRD 拟合、FT-IR 拟合与 BET 数据[5]，不包含力学平行数据。\n\n因此：8000 转针叶木的干纸抗张指数只能从 Figure 3(a) 读取近似值；但文中未说明该图是否带误差棒、误差棒对应几次重复，且本次我未查看该图，故不给读数。若要逐次平行原始值，需向作者索取原始记录。\n\n如果另有给出平行实验表格的文献（如中文制浆造纸期刊论文），可提供题名或关键词，我再协助定位。",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",

However, for the free OH(2) and OH(6) of hardwood fiber, the number of the free OH(2) and OH(6) decreased by 21.65% from 14.32% to 11.22%, with revolutions increasing from 0 r to 4000 r, followed by an increase of 45.37% in the stage of refining from 4000 r to 12,000 r, along with an decrease of 17.11%. It could be explained by the instability of free OH groups, which makes it easy to form new H-bonds, such as O(2)H· · · O(6) or O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>)H-bonds. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.",

In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. PFI2-027 这篇论文对干纸抗张性能有什么结论？另外请给出同一批样品的耐破指数和撕裂指数精确数据。

两版保留抗张提高及没有耐破/撕裂数值，新版删除背景和重复内容，未发现必答信息误删。

固定初稿
**干纸抗张性能的结论**

- 该论文（Li 等，2020，PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构与氢键的影响）发现：随着 PFI 打浆转数增加，干纸的抗张强度（以抗张指数表示）提高，主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加；同时，纸页的纤维间结合得到增强，因为纤维润胀（WRV 升高）使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有利于纤维网络结合 [14][11]。
- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆并未降低纤维本身的强度，即干纸强度的提高不是靠牺牲单根纤维强度换来的 [16]。
- 总体结论是：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化（尤其是内部纤丝化）程度、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且不伴随纤维抗张强度的下降 [17]。
- 方法上，干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定，零距抗张强度按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。

**关于耐破指数和撕裂指数**

这篇论文**没有报告耐破指数（burst index）和撕裂指数（tear index）**，因此无法给出“同一批样品”的这两项精确数据，也不应推测。文中涉及的力学指标只有抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度（分别对应图 3），测试标准也只提到 TAPPI T494、GB/T 12914-2008 和 ISO 15361，未涉及耐破度或撕裂度测试 [1][14]。若确需这两项数据，需要查阅该研究的补充材料（Online Resource）或其他批次/文献；但就目前检索到的正文与表格而言，没有相应数值。
旧复核
**干纸抗张性能的结论**

- 本论文（Li 等，2020，PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构与氢键的影响）发现：随着 PFI 打浆转数增加，干纸的抗张指数（tensile index）提高；作者把这一提高主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加（原文表述为“mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining”），并指出纤维润胀（WRV 升高）会使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有利于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度 [14][11][12]。
- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆并未降低纤维强度，该结果与 Kouko 等的报道一致 [16]。
- 总体结论：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化（尤其是内部纤丝化）程度、纤维润胀以及纸页的抗张强度，并且没有伴随纤维本身抗张强度的下降 [17]。
- 试验条件：干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定；湿纸幅强度按 GB/T 12914-2008 测定；零距抗张强度用 Pulmac Z-Span 2400 按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。样品为未打浆及 PFI 打浆（0、4000、8000、12,000、16,000 r）的针叶木和阔叶木纤维纸页 [14][18][5]。
- 需注意不确定性：正文只给出描述性趋势，没有报告具体抗张指数数值、标准差或统计检验；数值只体现在图 3 中（图 3 为按打浆转数绘制的曲线），而本次未能核实图中读数的精确值 [18]。此外，文中“抗张强度提高由纤丝化和细小纤维引起”属于作者的解释性归因，并非文中提供的定量因果验证。

**关于耐破指数和撕裂指数**

这篇论文并未报告耐破指数（burst index）和撕裂指数（tear index）。因此，无法给出“同一批样品”的这两项精确数据；这里也不应进行推测。文中涉及的力学指标只有抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度（见图 3）[14][18]；方法部分提到的标准也只有 TAPPI T494、GB/T 12914-2008 和 ISO 15361，未涉及耐破度或撕裂度测试 [1]。正文、表格（表 1、表 2 分别为结晶度/晶粒尺寸与氢键相对含量）中均无这两项数据 [5][4]。如果确需这两项数据，需要查阅该研究的补充材料（Online Resource，正文引用了 Table S1、Figures S1–S3）或其他批次/文献；但就目前检索到的材料而言，尚未解决这一数据缺口。
新复核
**干纸抗张性能的结论**

- PFI 打浆过程中，干纸的抗张强度（以抗张指数表示）随打浆转数增加而提高 [14]；作者把这一提高主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加 [14]。
- 作者还解释了纤维网络结合增强的原因：WRV 升高表明纤维润胀增加，纤维横向因此更柔顺，从而有利于纤维间结合强度提高 [11]。这些是作者的机理解释，不是通过分离变量证明的因果。
- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆没有降低纤维强度；作者据此认为，纸页抗张强度的提高并不是以纤维本身强度下降为代价 [16]。
- 作者的总体结论是：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化程度（尤其是内部纤丝化）和纤维润胀，并提高了纸页抗张强度，同时纤维抗张强度没有下降 [17]。
- 方法条件：干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定，零距抗张强度按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。

**关于耐破指数和撕裂指数**

这篇论文没有报告耐破指数和撕裂指数，因此无法给出同一批样品的这两项精确数据。文中涉及的力学指标只有抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度（图 3）[18][14]；测试标准只提到 TAPPI T494、GB/T 12914-2008 和 ISO 15361，未涉及耐破度或撕裂度测试 [1]。若需这两项数据，只能查该研究的补充材料或其他来源；就目前检索到的正文、图和表格而言，未发现相应数值，故不能提供或推测。

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1)."

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region.         "text": "**干纸抗张性能的结论**\n\n- 本论文（Li 等，2020，PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构与氢键的影响）发现：随着 PFI 打浆转数增加，干纸的抗张指数（tensile index）提高；作者把这一提高主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加（原文表述为“mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining”），并指出纤维润胀（WRV 升高）会使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有利于提高纤维网络的纤维间结合强度 [14][11][12]。\n- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆并未降低纤维强度，该结果与 Kouko 等的报道一致 [16]。\n- 总体结论：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化（尤其是内部纤丝化）程度、纤维润胀以及纸页的抗张强度，并且没有伴随纤维本身抗张强度的下降 [17]。\n- 试验条件：干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定；湿纸幅强度按 GB/T 12914-2008 测定；零距抗张强度用 Pulmac Z-Span 2400 按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。样品为未打浆及 PFI 打浆（0、4000、8000、12,000、16,000 r）的针叶木和阔叶木纤维纸页 [14][18][5]。\n- 需注意不确定性：正文只给出描述性趋势，没有报告具体抗张指数数值、标准差或统计检验；数值只体现在图 3 中（图 3 为按打浆转数绘制的曲线），而本次未能核实图中读数的精确值 [18]。此外，文中“抗张强度提高由纤丝化和细小纤维引起”属于作者的解释性归因，并非文中提供的定量因果验证。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "E14",
        "basis": {
          "type": "reference_evidence",
          "text": "In Figure 3, the tensile index, zero-span tensile index, and wet-web strength represented as a function of the refining revolutions. The increment of tensile strength is mainly caused by the increasing fibrillation and fines during PFI refining, as mentioned above. The wet–web strength of softwood fiber had a more significant increase when compared to that of hardwood fiber. It is for that fiber length plays an essential role in wet–web strength. The zero-span tensile index was usually used in characterizing the tensile strength of fibers. The results of the zero-span tensile index showed that PFI refining did not reduce fiber strength, which is consistent with the report of Kouko et al. [24]. The above results showed that PFI refining improved the extent of fibrillation (especially the internal fibrillation), the swelling of fibers, and the tensile strength of sheets without a decrease of the tensile strength of fibers."
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "C2",
        "text": "**关于耐破指数和撕裂指数**\n\n这篇论文并未报告耐破指数（burst index）和撕裂指数（tear index）。因此，无法给出“同一批样品”的这两项精确数据；这里也不应进行推测。文中涉及的力学指标只有抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度（见图 3）[14][18]；方法部分提到的标准也只有 TAPPI T494、GB/T 12914-2008 和 ISO 15361，未涉及耐破度或撕裂度测试 [1]。正文、表格（表 1、表 2 分别为结晶度/晶粒尺寸与氢键相对含量）中均无这两项数据 [5][4]。如果确需这两项数据，需要查阅该研究的补充材料（Online Resource，正文引用了 Table S1、Figures S1–S3）或其他批次/文献；但就目前检索到的材料而言，尚未解决这一数据缺口。",

          "text": "The fines content, weighted mean length, and macro-fibrillation index of each sample were determined with a MORFI LB analyzer (Techpap SAS, Grenoble, France). The tensile strength of dry sheets and Wet-web strength were tested according to TAPPI T494 and Chinese standard GBT 12914-2008, respectively. The zero-span tensile strength was tested with the Z-Span 2400 apparatus (Pulmac International Co. Ltd., Montpelier, VT, USA), according to the standard ISO 15361."

--- fixed draft
+++ new review
@@ -1,10 +1,11 @@
 **干纸抗张性能的结论**
 
-- 该论文（Li 等，2020，PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构与氢键的影响）发现：随着 PFI 打浆转数增加，干纸的抗张强度（以抗张指数表示）提高，主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加；同时，纸页的纤维间结合得到增强，因为纤维润胀（WRV 升高）使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有利于纤维网络结合 [14][11]。
-- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆并未降低纤维本身的强度，即干纸强度的提高不是靠牺牲单根纤维强度换来的 [16]。
-- 总体结论是：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化（尤其是内部纤丝化）程度、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且不伴随纤维抗张强度的下降 [17]。
-- 方法上，干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定，零距抗张强度按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。
+- PFI 打浆过程中，干纸的抗张强度（以抗张指数表示）随打浆转数增加而提高 [14]；作者把这一提高主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加 [14]。
+- 作者还解释了纤维网络结合增强的原因：WRV 升高表明纤维润胀增加，纤维横向因此更柔顺，从而有利于纤维间结合强度提高 [11]。这些是作者的机理解释，不是通过分离变量证明的因果。
+- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆没有降低纤维强度；作者据此认为，纸页抗张强度的提高并不是以纤维本身强度下降为代价 [16]。
+- 作者的总体结论是：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化程度（尤其是内部纤丝化）和纤维润胀，并提高了纸页抗张强度，同时纤维抗张强度没有下降 [17]。
+- 方法条件：干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定，零距抗张强度按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。
 
 **关于耐破指数和撕裂指数**
 
-这篇论文**没有报告耐破指数（burst index）和撕裂指数（tear index）**，因此无法给出“同一批样品”的这两项精确数据，也不应推测。文中涉及的力学指标只有抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度（分别对应图 3），测试标准也只提到 TAPPI T494、GB/T 12914-2008 和 ISO 15361，未涉及耐破度或撕裂度测试 [1][14]。若确需这两项数据，需要查阅该研究的补充材料（Online Resource）或其他批次/文献；但就目前检索到的正文与表格而言，没有相应数值。

  "fixed_draft": "**干纸抗张性能的结论**\n\n- 该论文（Li 等，2020，PFI 打浆对纤维素聚集结构与氢键的影响）发现：随着 PFI 打浆转数增加，干纸的抗张强度（以抗张指数表示）提高，主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加；同时，纸页的纤维间结合得到增强，因为纤维润胀（WRV 升高）使纤维在横向更柔顺，从而有利于纤维网络结合 [14][11]。\n- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆并未降低纤维本身的强度，即干纸强度的提高不是靠牺牲单根纤维强度换来的 [16]。\n- 总体结论是：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化（尤其是内部纤丝化）程度、纤维润胀和纸页抗张强度，且不伴随纤维抗张强度的下降 [17]。\n- 方法上，干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定，零距抗张强度按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。\n\n**关于耐破指数和撕裂指数**\n\n这篇论文**没有报告耐破指数（burst index）和撕裂指数（tear index）**，因此无法给出“同一批样品”的这两项精确数据，也不应推测。文中涉及的力学指标只有抗张指数、零距抗张指数和湿纸幅强度（分别对应图 3），测试标准也只提到 TAPPI T494、GB/T 12914-2008 和 ISO 15361，未涉及耐破度或撕裂度测试 [1][14]。若确需这两项数据，需要查阅该研究的补充材料（Online Resource）或其他批次/文献；但就目前检索到的正文与表格而言，没有相应数值。",

The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2.         "text": "**干纸抗张性能的结论**\n\n- PFI 打浆过程中，干纸的抗张强度（以抗张指数表示）随打浆转数增加而提高 [14]；作者把这一提高主要归因于打浆过程中纤丝化程度提高和细小纤维含量增加 [14]。\n- 作者还解释了纤维网络结合增强的原因：WRV 升高表明纤维润胀增加，纤维横向因此更柔顺，从而有利于纤维间结合强度提高 [11]。这些是作者的机理解释，不是通过分离变量证明的因果。\n- 零距抗张指数结果表明，PFI 打浆没有降低纤维强度；作者据此认为，纸页抗张强度的提高并不是以纤维本身强度下降为代价 [16]。\n- 作者的总体结论是：PFI 打浆提高了纤丝化程度（尤其是内部纤丝化）和纤维润胀，并提高了纸页抗张强度，同时纤维抗张强度没有下降 [17]。\n- 方法条件：干纸抗张强度按 TAPPI T494 测定，零距抗张强度按 ISO 15361 测定 [1]。",

PFI2-028 请比较这篇PFI论文与《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》的全部实验数据，给出两篇共同结论。

两版仍把O2只在首段增加写入；新版又写先升后降再升，自相矛盾。旧版新增0转与16SR不一致的错误，新版去掉了这句。

固定初稿
我已完成两次检索（已达到本题允许的检索上限），但两次检索只返回了 PFI 论文（Li 2020，doc_0fcf2a50cfa02d21），**《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》在本次可用文献库中没有被检索到**，因此我无法取得该文的实验数据（纤维长度、宽厚比、细胞壁厚度、Runkel 比等与纸浆抗张/耐破/撕裂指数的关系）。据此，我不能给出“两篇论文的全部实验数据比较”及“共同结论”——若强行给出即为猜测。

下面只陈述有证据支持的 PFI 论文结论，并标明缺口（无法归入“共同结论”）。

**PFI 论文的实验条件（仅针叶/阔叶漂白硫酸盐浆）**
- 打浆：PFI 磨，浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶浆）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶浆），转数 0/4000/8000/12000/16000 r；对应打浆度分别 16→79 °SR（针叶）与 0/26/40/57/70 °SR（阔叶）[1]。

**主要结果**
- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度下降、针叶浆细小纤维含量上升；针叶浆变化显著，阔叶浆这两项相对不显著（作者归因于其打浆压力更低）[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，源于纤丝化产生的新表面与孔隙[5]。
- 强度：湿纸幅强度上升（针叶浆增幅更明显，纤维长度起关键作用）；零距抗张表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维本身强度；干纸页抗张强度提高[5]。
- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶），两者显著相关（r = 0.919 与 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。
- 氢键网络：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降（仅 0→4000 r 阶段上升）[8]。
- 核心结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，故打浆中可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与氢键含量变化不大，故认为 PFI 打浆是“以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小”的温和机械处理[7]。

**未解决的缺口**
1. 非木材纤维那篇文献的原始表格/图（各类非木材原料的纤维指标与手抄片强度指标、回归或相关性系数、样本量）均未获得；
2. 因而无法判断两文是否在“纤维长度/细纤维含量与抗张强度正相关”这类命题上一致，也无法核对是否存在相反的因果或相关报道；
3. 本回答中所有数值仅为 PFI 论文自身的相对变化，不能当作两文共同结论或普适规律。

如果您能提供该非木材纤维文献的 PDF/DOI 或它在库中的文档名，我可以再做逐表逐图对比并给出真正意义上的共同结论。
旧复核
**审稿说明：本回答基于两次检索中实际获得的文献证据，未查看任何图像像素。两次检索均未返回《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》，该文在本次可用文献库中不可得；因此无法进行“两篇论文全部实验数据的比较”，也无法给出经数据核对的“共同结论”。**

**一、不可解决的缺口**
1. 非木材纤维文献的原始表格或图（各原料的纤维长度、宽厚比、细胞壁厚度、Runkel 比等纤维指标，与纸浆抗张、耐破、撕裂指数的对应值），以及回归、相关系数、样本量、制浆与打浆条件，均未被检索到，因而缺失。
2. 由于缺少上述数据，无法判定两篇论文是否在“纤维长度、细小纤维与抗张强度关系”等命题上一致，也无法确认是否存在相反的报道。
3. 因此，下述内容只属于 PFI 论文自身的报道（其中数值是相对变化），不能表述为两篇论文的共同结论或普适规律。

**二、PFI 论文的实验条件（仅针叶/阔叶漂白硫酸盐浆）**
- 纤维为国产商品漂白硫酸盐浆（针叶/阔叶）；采用 PFI 磨（Hamjern Maskin A/S），按 Tappi T248 wd-97，浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶）[1]。
- 转数 0/4000/8000/12000/16000 r；对应打浆度（ISO 5267-1，Schopper Riegler）针叶浆为 16、20、40、63、79 °SR，阔叶浆为 0、26、40、57、70 °SR[1]。注意：原文对两组均写作“0、4000、8000、12000、16000 r”，但针叶浆给出的打浆度最低值为 16 °SR 而非 0，原文表述存在不一致，未加解释。

**三、PFI 论文的主要结果（相对量）**
- 形态：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量上升；针叶浆这两项变化显著，阔叶浆则相对不显著。作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力更低，这是作者的解释性推断，并非独立验证的因果结论[5]。
- 润胀与比表面：打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者归因于纤丝化产生的新的表面与孔隙（比表面与孔结构数据在补充材料 Table S1，正文未给出数值）[5]。
- 强度：湿纸幅强度上升，针叶浆增幅更明显，作者以纤维长度起关键作用解释；零距抗张指数表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度；干纸页抗张强度提高[5]。上述均为变化方向与相对比较，按证据未给出具体数值。
- 结晶区：纤维素晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66% 与 15.47%（针叶）、2.65% 与 19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关，r = 0.919（针叶）与 0.925（阔叶），p < 0.05；微晶尺寸变化很小（原文表列约 2.9–4.8 nm，随晶面与转数小幅波动）[9]。原文同时指出 CI-XI 明显高于 CI-XA，可能源于无定形贡献拟合过度，因此两指数的绝对值不宜直接比较[9]。
- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 总体上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降（仅 0→4000 r 阶段上升）。原文强调这些氢键既有断裂也有生成，趋势呈阶段性波动[8]。
- 结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，作者据此推测打浆中可由 CI-XI 估计该氢键趋势；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与氢键含量变化不大，故作者认为 PFI 打浆是“以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小”的温和处理[7]。此处“相关”为统计相关，“温和、破坏较小”为作者基于变化幅度的判断。

**四、结论**
在缺少非木材纤维文献数据的前提下，唯一有据可陈的是上述 PFI 论文结果；任何“两文共同结论”的表述均无证据支持。若需完成比较，请提供该文献的 PDF、DOI 或库内文档名。

下面只陈述有证据支持的 PFI 论文内容；这些内容单独不构成“共同结论”。

**实验条件（仅针叶材与阔叶材漂白硫酸盐浆）**
- PFI 磨打浆：浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶浆）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶浆），转数取 0、4000、8000、12,000、16,000 r 共 5 个水平；对应打浆度约 16、20、40、63、79 °SR（针叶浆）与 0、26、40、57、70 °SR（阔叶浆）[1]。

**主要结果**
- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量呈上升趋势；针叶浆这两项变化显著，而阔叶浆的这两项变化相对于针叶浆不显著；作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力较低，这是作者的解释，并非已验证的因果关系[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者认为这是纤丝化产生新表面与孔隙造成的[5]。
- 强度：干纸页抗张强度提高，湿纸幅强度上升；针叶浆在湿纸幅强度上的增幅更明显，作者认为纤维长度起关键作用[5]。零距抗张结果表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度[5]；这并不排除纤维强度在其他方面或更高打浆程度下发生变化。
- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关（针叶 r = 0.919、阔叶 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。
- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降，仅在 0→4000 r 阶段上升[8]。上述变化并非单调：O(6)H···O(3′) 先降后升再降，O(2)H···O(6) 先升后降再升，O(3)H···O(5) 先升、小幅降、再升[8]。
- 作者结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，因此作者提出打浆时可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势（这是相关关系上的推测，非因果证明）；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与各类氢键含量变化不大，作者据此认为 PFI 打浆是以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小的温和机械处理[7]。

**未能确定的事项**
1. 非木材纤维论文的原始数据（纤维指标、纸浆强度指标、回归/相关系数、样本量）均未获得，因此无法核对其处理水平与样本量的对应关系；
2. 因而无法判断两文在“纤维长度、细小纤维含量与抗张强度关系”等命题上是否一致，也无法核对是否存在相反的报道；
3. 本文数值均为 PFI 论文自身的相对变化，且只涉及针叶材与阔叶材漂白硫酸盐浆，不可外推为非木材纤维的规律，也不能作为两文共同结论。

如能提供该非木材纤维文献的 PDF、DOI 或库中文档名，可再做逐表逐图对比并给出真正的共同结论。

  "fixed_draft": "我已完成两次检索（已达到本题允许的检索上限），但两次检索只返回了 PFI 论文（Li 2020，doc_0fcf2a50cfa02d21），**《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》在本次可用文献库中没有被检索到**，因此我无法取得该文的实验数据（纤维长度、宽厚比、细胞壁厚度、Runkel 比等与纸浆抗张/耐破/撕裂指数的关系）。据此，我不能给出“两篇论文的全部实验数据比较”及“共同结论”——若强行给出即为猜测。\n\n下面只陈述有证据支持的 PFI 论文结论，并标明缺口（无法归入“共同结论”）。\n\n**PFI 论文的实验条件（仅针叶/阔叶漂白硫酸盐浆）**\n- 打浆：PFI 磨，浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶浆）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶浆），转数 0/4000/8000/12000/16000 r；对应打浆度分别 16→79 °SR（针叶）与 0/26/40/57/70 °SR（阔叶）[1]。\n\n**主要结果**\n- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度下降、针叶浆细小纤维含量上升；针叶浆变化显著，阔叶浆这两项相对不显著（作者归因于其打浆压力更低）[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，源于纤丝化产生的新表面与孔隙[5]。\n- 强度：湿纸幅强度上升（针叶浆增幅更明显，纤维长度起关键作用）；零距抗张表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维本身强度；干纸页抗张强度提高[5]。\n- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶），两者显著相关（r = 0.919 与 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。\n- 氢键网络：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降（仅 0→4000 r 阶段上升）[8]。\n- 核心结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，故打浆中可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与氢键含量变化不大，故认为 PFI 打浆是“以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小”的温和机械处理[7]。\n\n**未解决的缺口**\n1. 非木材纤维那篇文献的原始表格/图（各类非木材原料的纤维指标与手抄片强度指标、回归或相关性系数、样本量）均未获得；\n2. 因而无法判断两文是否在“纤维长度/细纤维含量与抗张强度正相关”这类命题上一致，也无法核对是否存在相反的因果或相关报道；\n3. 本回答中所有数值仅为 PFI 论文自身的相对变化，不能当作两文共同结论或普适规律。\n\n如果您能提供该非木材纤维文献的 PDF/DOI 或它在库中的文档名，我可以再做逐表逐图对比并给出真正意义上的共同结论。",

    "answer": "**审稿说明：本回答基于两次检索中实际获得的文献证据，未查看任何图像像素。两次检索均未返回《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》，该文在本次可用文献库中不可得；因此无法进行“两篇论文全部实验数据的比较”，也无法给出经数据核对的“共同结论”。**\n\n**一、不可解决的缺口**\n1. 非木材纤维文献的原始表格或图（各原料的纤维长度、宽厚比、细胞壁厚度、Runkel 比等纤维指标，与纸浆抗张、耐破、撕裂指数的对应值），以及回归、相关系数、样本量、制浆与打浆条件，均未被检索到，因而缺失。\n2. 由于缺少上述数据，无法判定两篇论文是否在“纤维长度、细小纤维与抗张强度关系”等命题上一致，也无法确认是否存在相反的报道。\n3. 因此，下述内容只属于 PFI 论文自身的报道（其中数值是相对变化），不能表述为两篇论文的共同结论或普适规律。\n\n**二、PFI 论文的实验条件（仅针叶/阔叶漂白硫酸盐浆）**\n- 纤维为国产商品漂白硫酸盐浆（针叶/阔叶）；采用 PFI 磨（Hamjern Maskin A/S），按 Tappi T248 wd-97，浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶）[1]。\n- 转数 0/4000/8000/12000/16000 r；对应打浆度（ISO 5267-1，Schopper Riegler）针叶浆为 16、20、40、63、79 °SR，阔叶浆为 0、26、40、57、70 °SR[1]。注意：原文对两组均写作“0、4000、8000、12000、16000 r”，但针叶浆给出的打浆度最低值为 16 °SR 而非 0，原文表述存在不一致，未加解释。\n\n**三、PFI 论文的主要结果（相对量）**\n- 形态：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量上升；针叶浆这两项变化显著，阔叶浆则相对不显著。作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力更低，这是作者的解释性推断，并非独立验证的因果结论[5]。\n- 润胀与比表面：打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者归因于纤丝化产生的新的表面与孔隙（比表面与孔结构数据在补充材料 Table S1，正文未给出数值）[5]。\n- 强度：湿纸幅强度上升，针叶浆增幅更明显，作者以纤维长度起关键作用解释；零距抗张指数表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度；干纸页抗张强度提高[5]。上述均为变化方向与相对比较，按证据未给出具体数值。\n- 结晶区：纤维素晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66% 与 15.47%（针叶）、2.65% 与 19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关，r = 0.919（针叶）与 0.925（阔叶），p < 0.05；微晶尺寸变化很小（原文表列约 2.9–4.8 nm，随晶面与转数小幅波动）[9]。原文同时指出 CI-XI 明显高于 CI-XA，可能源于无定形贡献拟合过度，因此两指数的绝对值不宜直接比较[9]。\n- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 总体上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降（仅 0→4000 r 阶段上升）。原文强调这些氢键既有断裂也有生成，趋势呈阶段性波动[8]。\n- 结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，作者据此推测打浆中可由 CI-XI 估计该氢键趋势；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与氢键含量变化不大，故作者认为 PFI 打浆是“以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小”的温和处理[7]。此处“相关”为统计相关，“温和、破坏较小”为作者基于变化幅度的判断。\n\n**四、结论**\n在缺少非木材纤维文献数据的前提下，唯一有据可陈的是上述 PFI 论文结果；任何“两文共同结论”的表述均无证据支持。若需完成比较，请提供该文献的 PDF、DOI 或库内文档名。",

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds.",

        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",
        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] References\n[原文]\n1. Gharehkhani, S.; Sadeghinezhad, E.; Kazi, S.N.; Yarmand, H.; Badarudin, A.; Safaei, M.R.; Zubir, M.N.M. Basic efects of pulp refining on fiber properties—A review. Carbohydr. Polym. 2015, 115, 785–803. [CrossRef] [PubMed]",
        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.",

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3.       {
        "id": "C3",
        "text": "**三、PFI 论文的主要结果（相对量）**\n- 形态：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量上升；针叶浆这两项变化显著，阔叶浆则相对不显著。作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力更低，这是作者的解释性推断，并非独立验证的因果结论[5]。\n- 润胀与比表面：打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者归因于纤丝化产生的新的表面与孔隙（比表面与孔结构数据在补充材料 Table S1，正文未给出数值）[5]。\n- 强度：湿纸幅强度上升，针叶浆增幅更明显，作者以纤维长度起关键作用解释；零距抗张指数表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度；干纸页抗张强度提高[5]。上述均为变化方向与相对比较，按证据未给出具体数值。\n- 结晶区：纤维素晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66% 与 15.47%（针叶）、2.65% 与 19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关，r = 0.919（针叶）与 0.925（阔叶），p < 0.05；微晶尺寸变化很小（原文表列约 2.9–4.8 nm，随晶面与转数小幅波动）[9]。原文同时指出 CI-XI 明显高于 CI-XA，可能源于无定形贡献拟合过度，因此两指数的绝对值不宜直接比较[9]。\n- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 总体上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降（仅 0→4000 r 阶段上升）。原文强调这些氢键既有断裂也有生成，趋势呈阶段性波动[8]。\n- 结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，作者据此推测打浆中可由 CI-XI 估计该氢键趋势；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与氢键含量变化不大，故作者认为 PFI 打浆是“以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小”的温和处理[7]。此处“相关”为统计相关，“温和、破坏较小”为作者基于变化幅度的判断。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null

+我检索了两次（已达到本题允许的检索上限），但两次检索都只返回了 PFI 论文（Li 2020，doc_0fcf2a50cfa02d21）；**因此无法从本次可用文献库中检索到《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》，也拿不到它的实验数据**（比如各类非木材原料的纤维长度、宽厚比、细胞壁厚度等指标，以及这些指标与纸浆抗张、耐破、撕裂指数之间的表格、相关性系数或样本量）。因此**无法比较这两篇论文的全部实验数据，也无法给出共同结论**；如果强行给出，就只能是猜测。
 
-下面只陈述有证据支持的 PFI 论文结论，并标明缺口（无法归入“共同结论”）。
+下面只陈述有证据支持的 PFI 论文内容；这些内容单独不构成“共同结论”。
 
-**PFI 论文的实验条件（仅针叶/阔叶漂白硫酸盐浆）**
-- 打浆：PFI 磨，浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶浆）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶浆），转数 0/4000/8000/12000/16000 r；对应打浆度分别 16→79 °SR（针叶）与 0/26/40/57/70 °SR（阔叶）[1]。
+**实验条件（仅针叶材与阔叶材漂白硫酸盐浆）**
+- PFI 磨打浆：浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶浆）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶浆），转数取 0、4000、8000、12,000、16,000 r 共 5 个水平；对应打浆度约 16、20、40、63、79 °SR（针叶浆）与 0、26、40、57、70 °SR（阔叶浆）[1]。
 
 **主要结果**
-- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度下降、针叶浆细小纤维含量上升；针叶浆变化显著，阔叶浆这两项相对不显著（作者归因于其打浆压力更低）[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，源于纤丝化产生的新表面与孔隙[5]。
-- 强度：湿纸幅强度上升（针叶浆增幅更明显，纤维长度起关键作用）；零距抗张表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维本身强度；干纸页抗张强度提高[5]。
-- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶），两者显著相关（r = 0.919 与 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。
-- 氢键网络：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降（仅 0→4000 r 阶段上升）[8]。
-- 核心结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，故打浆中可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与氢键含量变化不大，故认为 PFI 打浆是“以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小”的温和机械处理[7]。
+- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量呈上升趋势；针叶浆这两项变化显著，而阔叶浆的这两项变化相对于针叶浆不显著；作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力较低，这是作者的解释，并非已验证的因果关系[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者认为这是纤丝化产生新表面与孔隙造成的[5]。
+- 强度：干纸页抗张强度提高，湿纸幅强度上升；针叶浆在湿纸幅强度上的增幅更明显，作者认为纤维长度起关键作用[5]。零距抗张结果表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度[5]；这并不排除纤维强度在其他方面或更高打浆程度下发生变化。
+- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关（针叶 r = 0.919、阔叶 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。
+- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降，仅在 0→4000 r 阶段上升[8]。上述变化并非单调：O(6)H···O(3′) 先降后升再降，O(2)H···O(6) 先升后降再升，O(3)H···O(5) 先升、小幅降、再升[8]。
+- 作者结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，因此作者提出打浆时可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势（这是相关关系上的推测，非因果证明）；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与各类氢键含量变化不大，作者据此认为 PFI 打浆是以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小的温和机械处理[7]。
 
-**未解决的缺口**
-1. 非木材纤维那篇文献的原始表格/图（各类非木材原料的纤维指标与手抄片强度指标、回归或相关性系数、样本量）均未获得；
-2. 因而无法判断两文是否在“纤维长度/细纤维含量与抗张强度正相关”这类命题上一致，也无法核对是否存在相反的因果或相关报道；
-3. 本回答中所有数值仅为 PFI 论文自身的相对变化，不能当作两文共同结论或普适规律。
+**未能确定的事项**
+1. 非木材纤维论文的原始数据（纤维指标、纸浆强度指标、回归/相关系数、样本量）均未获得，因此无法核对其处理水平与样本量的对应关系；
+2. 因而无法判断两文在“纤维长度、细小纤维含量与抗张强度关系”等命题上是否一致，也无法核对是否存在相反的报道；
+3. 本文数值均为 PFI 论文自身的相对变化，且只涉及针叶材与阔叶材漂白硫酸盐浆，不可外推为非木材纤维的规律，也不能作为两文共同结论。
 
-如果您能提供该非木材纤维文献的 PDF/DOI 或它在库中的文档名，我可以再做逐表逐图对比并给出真正意义上的共同结论。

    "answer": "我检索了两次（已达到本题允许的检索上限），但两次检索都只返回了 PFI 论文（Li 2020，doc_0fcf2a50cfa02d21）；**因此无法从本次可用文献库中检索到《Non-Wood Fibers: Relationships of Fiber Properties with Pulp Properties》，也拿不到它的实验数据**（比如各类非木材原料的纤维长度、宽厚比、细胞壁厚度等指标，以及这些指标与纸浆抗张、耐破、撕裂指数之间的表格、相关性系数或样本量）。因此**无法比较这两篇论文的全部实验数据，也无法给出共同结论**；如果强行给出，就只能是猜测。\n\n下面只陈述有证据支持的 PFI 论文内容；这些内容单独不构成“共同结论”。\n\n**实验条件（仅针叶材与阔叶材漂白硫酸盐浆）**\n- PFI 磨打浆：浆浓 10%，盘间隙 0.2 mm，比压 3.33 N/mm（针叶浆）与 1.77 N/mm（阔叶浆），转数取 0、4000、8000、12,000、16,000 r 共 5 个水平；对应打浆度约 16、20、40、63、79 °SR（针叶浆）与 0、26、40、57、70 °SR（阔叶浆）[1]。\n\n**主要结果**\n- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量呈上升趋势；针叶浆这两项变化显著，而阔叶浆的这两项变化相对于针叶浆不显著；作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力较低，这是作者的解释，并非已验证的因果关系[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者认为这是纤丝化产生新表面与孔隙造成的[5]。\n- 强度：干纸页抗张强度提高，湿纸幅强度上升；针叶浆在湿纸幅强度上的增幅更明显，作者认为纤维长度起关键作用[5]。零距抗张结果表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度[5]；这并不排除纤维强度在其他方面或更高打浆程度下发生变化。\n- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关（针叶 r = 0.919、阔叶 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。\n- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降，仅在 0→4000 r 阶段上升[8]。上述变化并非单调：O(6)H···O(3′) 先降后升再降，O(2)H···O(6) 先升后降再升，O(3)H···O(5) 先升、小幅降、再升[8]。\n- 作者结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，因此作者提出打浆时可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势（这是相关关系上的推测，非因果证明）；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与各类氢键含量变化不大，作者据此认为 PFI 打浆是以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小的温和机械处理[7]。\n\n**未能确定的事项**\n1. 非木材纤维论文的原始数据（纤维指标、纸浆强度指标、回归/相关系数、样本量）均未获得，因此无法核对其处理水平与样本量的对应关系；\n2. 因而无法判断两文在“纤维长度、细小纤维含量与抗张强度关系”等命题上是否一致，也无法核对是否存在相反的报道；\n3. 本文数值均为 PFI 论文自身的相对变化，且只涉及针叶材与阔叶材漂白硫酸盐浆，不可外推为非木材纤维的规律，也不能作为两文共同结论。\n\n如能提供该非木材纤维文献的 PDF、DOI 或库中文档名，可再做逐表逐图对比并给出真正的共同结论。",

Conclusions\n[原文]\nupramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.PFI refining acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of thethe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure."

Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure."

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nFor the content of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the trend can be <sup>For</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>content</sup> <sup>of</sup> <sup>O(6)H O(3′)</sup> <sup>inter-molecular</sup> <sup>H-bonds</sup> <sup>of</sup> <sup>softwood</sup> <sup>fiber,</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>trend</sup> <sup>can</sup> <sup>be</sup>divided into two stages, as shown in Table 2a. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds of <sup>with</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>revolutions</sup> <sup>increasing</sup> <sup>from</sup> <sup>8000</sup> <sup>r</sup> <sup>to</sup> <sup>16,000</sup> <sup>r.</sup> <sup>Regarding</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>O(6)H O(3′)</sup> <sup>H-bonds</sup> <sup>of</sup>hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nAs to the O(3)H· · · O(5) intra-molecular H-bonds of softwood fiber, the content had a growth of 10.09% from 28.44% to 31.31% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r, and then had a slight decrease of 1.44% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by an increase of 13.16% until the end of refining. Overall, the trend was similar to that of hardwood fibers, which first increased and then had a decrease, followed by a growth. During the whole refining, the amount of $\\mathrm { O } ( 3 ) \\mathrm { H } \\cdots \\mathrm { O } ( 5 )$ H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers showed an upward tendency and increased by 22.78% and 8.8%, respectively. The increase might be because the stable O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds might have not only less breakage under the action of water as destructor to the crystallites [30], but also creation in the amorphous region upon drying. Because hydrogen bond–covalent bond synergies play an important role in the cellulose stifness axial modulus, more O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds will enhance the cellulose stifness [33,34].\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nIn the case of the O(2)H· · · O(6) intra-molecular H-bonds for softwood fiber, the trend of content can be described as two phases. It had an increase of 3.5% from 31.4% to 32.5% in the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r and it then decreased by 21.57% from 4000 r to 12000 r, along with a growth of 15.26% in the last refining stage. For the content of the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds of hardwood fiber, it increased firstly and then had a decrease that was also followed by an increase. For both fibers, the content of O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds decreased, except for the stage of refining from 0 r to 4000 r. It might be due to the fact that the O(2)H· · · O(6) H-bonds, which are much more accessible to water, are less stable than O(3)H· · · O(5) H-bonds."

        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 2. Methods > 2.1. PFI Refining\n[原文]\nCommercial bleached softwood and hardwood kraft pulp fibers were obtained from Zhongzhirenhe Company (Jinan, Shandong Province, China). Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",
        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] References\n[原文]\n1. Gharehkhani, S.; Sadeghinezhad, E.; Kazi, S.N.; Yarmand, H.; Badarudin, A.; Safaei, M.R.; Zubir, M.N.M. Basic efects of pulp refining on fiber properties—A review. Carbohydr. Polym. 2015, 115, 785–803. [CrossRef] [PubMed]",
        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure.",

        "text": "**主要结果**\n- 形态与润胀：两种浆的宏观纤丝化指数与纤维长度均呈下降趋势，针叶浆细小纤维含量呈上升趋势；针叶浆这两项变化显著，而阔叶浆的这两项变化相对于针叶浆不显著；作者将其归因于阔叶浆所用打浆压力较低，这是作者的解释，并非已验证的因果关系[5]。打浆度与 WRV 随转数显著上升，作者认为这是纤丝化产生新表面与孔隙造成的[5]。\n- 强度：干纸页抗张强度提高，湿纸幅强度上升；针叶浆在湿纸幅强度上的增幅更明显，作者认为纤维长度起关键作用[5]。零距抗张结果表明 PFI 打浆未降低纤维强度[5]；这并不排除纤维强度在其他方面或更高打浆程度下发生变化。\n- 结晶区：晶型未变；CI-XI 与 CI-XA 分别下降 4.66%/15.47%（针叶）与 2.65%/19.4%（阔叶）；两种指数显著相关（针叶 r = 0.919、阔叶 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）；微晶尺寸变化很小（约 3.0–4.8 nm）[9]。\n- 氢键：O(6)H···O(3′) 含量总体下降 16.54%（针叶）与 5.91%（阔叶）；O(3)H···O(5) 上升 22.78% 与 8.8%；O(2)H···O(6) 总体下降，仅在 0→4000 r 阶段上升[8]。上述变化并非单调：O(6)H···O(3′) 先降后升再降，O(2)H···O(6) 先升后降再升，O(3)H···O(5) 先升、小幅降、再升[8]。\n- 作者结论：纤丝化与纤维性能变化同超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）变化相关；CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 含量显著正相关，因此作者提出打浆时可由 CI-XI 推测该氢键趋势（这是相关关系上的推测，非因果证明）；总体结晶度、微晶尺寸与各类氢键含量变化不大，作者据此认为 PFI 打浆是以纤丝化为主、对超分子结构破坏较小的温和机械处理[7]。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },

PFI2-029 本文已经训练好的纸张抗张预测模型，其验证集R²和RMSE是多少？请给出最佳模型名称。

旧版将CI-XI/CI-XA的0.919/0.925错配为氢键相关，并把T494带到零距；新版正确分开测试标准并去掉错配相关系数，必要拒答保留。

固定初稿
无法回答该问题——“本文已训练好的纸张抗张预测模型”在当前可检索文献中并不存在。

核查情况：
- 两次检索（已达每次问答上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。
- 该文只做实验表征：纤维形态、打浆度/WRV、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸、FT-IR 氢键解析，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度 [2][5]；全文没有任何机器学习/统计预测模型的训练、验证集划分或最佳模型比较。
- 该文中出现的 R²（如 0.9995）是 FT-IR 谱峰非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非模型验证集 R²；其结论章节也仅讨论超分子结构变化与 CI-XI–氢键含量的相关性，未涉及建模 [11][12]。
- 因此“验证集 R²、RMSE 数值”与“最佳模型名称”在现有证据中均缺失，我不能凭猜测给出具体数值或模型名。

建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作，告知文献信息后我可再核对验证集指标与最佳模型名称。
旧复核
无法回答该问题——“本文已训练好的纸张抗张预测模型”在当前可检索文献中并不存在。

核查情况：
- 两次检索（已达每次问答上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li 等（2020）关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7][8]。
- 该文只做实验表征：纤维形态、打浆度/WRV、XRD 结晶度（CI-XI、CI-XA）与微晶尺寸、FT-IR 氢键解析，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度、零距抗张强度 [2][5][9]；全文没有任何机器学习/统计预测模型的训练、验证集划分或最佳模型比较。
- 该文中出现的 R²（如软木浆 0.9995–0.9996、阔叶木浆 0.9989–0.9992）是 FT-IR 羟基谱带非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非模型验证集 R²；其结论章节仅讨论超分子结构变化以及 CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量之间的相关性（相关系数 0.919/0.925，p<0.05），未涉及建模 [10][11][12]。
- 因此“验证集 R²、RMSE 数值”与“最佳模型名称”在现有证据中均缺失；文中未报告任何预测性能指标，我也不能凭猜测给出具体数值或模型名。

建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作（如使用 XGBoost、随机森林、深度学习等），告知文献信息后我可再核对验证集 R²、RMSE 及最佳模型名称。

核查情况：
- 两次检索（已达每次问答的检索上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。
- 该文为实验表征类研究，内容涉及纤维形态与打浆度/WRV [1]、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸 [5]、FT-IR 氢键解析 [3]，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度、按 GBT 12914-2008 测湿纸幅强度、按 ISO 15361 测零距抗张强度 [2]。其中没有机器学习或统计预测模型的训练过程、验证集划分，也没有模型间的比较与“最佳模型”的选择。
- 该文中出现的 R²（如软木纤维各磨浆转数下为 0.9995–0.9996）是 FT-IR 羟基谱带非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非预测模型验证集上的 R²，二者不可混用。
- 该文结论部分讨论的是 PFI 磨浆过程中超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）的变化，以及 CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量之间的正相关（该相关仅在所研究的软木与硬木浆、0–16,000 转 PFI 磨浆条件下成立，属相关性而非因果，原文亦仅以“might be generally speculated”表述推测）[11][12]。这些都不是预测模型结果。

建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作，请告知文献信息，我可再核对其验证集指标与最佳模型名称。

Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\nA mixture of inter-molecular and intra-molecular H-bonds is considered to be the cause for the broadening of OH bands in the FT-IR spectra. According to the formulae of H-bonding energy and H-bonding distance (Equations (4) and (5)), the H-bonding energies and H-bonding distances of the three H-bonds remained unchanged, as the peak positions of three H-bonds almost did not exhibit red shift or blue shift. It decreased by 7.72% from 28.23% to 26.05% as refining from 0r to 4000 r and then increased by 9.14% from 4000 r to 8000 r, followed by a decrease of 17.13%, with the revolutions increasing from 8000 r to 16,000 r. Regarding the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds of <sup>with</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>revolutions</sup> <sup>increasing</sup> <sup>from</sup> <sup>8000</sup> <sup>r</sup> <sup>to</sup> <sup>16,000</sup> <sup>r.</sup> <sup>Regarding</sup> <sup>the</sup> <sup>O(6)H O(3′)</sup> <sup>H-bonds</sup> <sup>of</sup>hardwood fiber, the trend was almost similar to that of softwood fibers, except for a small increase of 0.45% from 8000 r to 12,000 r (in Table 2b).\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.3. Efect of PFI Refining on H-Bonding Energies, H-Bonding Distances, and Content of H-Bonds\n[原文]\n On the whole, the amount of the O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers decreased by 16.54% and 5.91% altogether, respectively. The decrease might be due to the cleavage among cellulose molecular chains under the mechanical action of PFI refining, which was closely related to internal and external fibrillation (as seen in Section 3.1). On the other hand, the increase illustrates that there was not only the breakage, but also the formation of O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds. Both the fewer inter-molecular H-bonds and the lower CI (as Section 3.2 shows) will further improve the flexibility of cellulosic fibers, due to the higher mobility of molecular chains, the accessibility, and the WRV of fibers (as seen in Section 3.1)."

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Two pulp were treated with a PFI refiner (Hamjern Maskin A/S, Hamar, Norway) according to Tappi T248 wd-97, with a pulp consistency of 10%, the gap between the opposite refining plates was 0.2 mm, and forces per bar length were 3.33 N/mm and 1.77 N/mm for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers, respectively. The drainability was characterized by the Schopper Riegler number (SR-number) with the standards ISO 5267-1. Two pulp fibers were separately refined in a PFI refiner at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions and at 0, 4000, 8000, 12,000, and 16,000 revolutions, respectively. Corresponding various pulps with an increasing beating degree, such as 16, 20, 40, 63, and 79<sup>◦</sup> SR, were obtained for softwood fibers and 0, 26, 40, 57, and 70<sup>◦</sup> SR were obtained for hardwood fibers.",
