 核查情况：
-- 两次检索（已达每次问答上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。
-- 该文只做实验表征：纤维形态、打浆度/WRV、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸、FT-IR 氢键解析，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度 [2][5]；全文没有任何机器学习/统计预测模型的训练、验证集划分或最佳模型比较。
-- 该文中出现的 R²（如 0.9995）是 FT-IR 谱峰非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非模型验证集 R²；其结论章节也仅讨论超分子结构变化与 CI-XI–氢键含量的相关性，未涉及建模 [11][12]。
-- 因此“验证集 R²、RMSE 数值”与“最佳模型名称”在现有证据中均缺失，我不能凭猜测给出具体数值或模型名。
+- 两次检索（已达每次问答的检索上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。
+- 该文为实验表征类研究，内容涉及纤维形态与打浆度/WRV [1]、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸 [5]、FT-IR 氢键解析 [3]，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度、按 GBT 12914-2008 测湿纸幅强度、按 ISO 15361 测零距抗张强度 [2]。其中没有机器学习或统计预测模型的训练过程、验证集划分，也没有模型间的比较与“最佳模型”的选择。
+- 该文中出现的 R²（如软木纤维各磨浆转数下为 0.9995–0.9996）是 FT-IR 羟基谱带非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非预测模型验证集上的 R²，二者不可混用。
+- 该文结论部分讨论的是 PFI 磨浆过程中超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）的变化，以及 CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量之间的正相关（该相关仅在所研究的软木与硬木浆、0–16,000 转 PFI 磨浆条件下成立，属相关性而非因果，原文亦仅以“might be generally speculated”表述推测）[11][12]。这些都不是预测模型结果。
 
-建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作，告知文献信息后我可再核对验证集指标与最佳模型名称。
+建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作，请告知文献信息，我可再核对其验证集指标与最佳模型名称。

  "fixed_draft": "无法回答该问题——“本文已训练好的纸张抗张预测模型”在当前可检索文献中并不存在。\n\n核查情况：\n- 两次检索（已达每次问答上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。\n- 该文只做实验表征：纤维形态、打浆度/WRV、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸、FT-IR 氢键解析，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度 [2][5]；全文没有任何机器学习/统计预测模型的训练、验证集划分或最佳模型比较。\n- 该文中出现的 R²（如 0.9995）是 FT-IR 谱峰非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非模型验证集 R²；其结论章节也仅讨论超分子结构变化与 CI-XI–氢键含量的相关性，未涉及建模 [11][12]。\n- 因此“验证集 R²、RMSE 数值”与“最佳模型名称”在现有证据中均缺失，我不能凭猜测给出具体数值或模型名。\n\n建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作，告知文献信息后我可再核对验证集指标与最佳模型名称。",

    "answer": "无法给出所问的数值——“本文已训练好的纸张抗张预测模型”在当前可获得的证据中并不存在，因此验证集 R²、RMSE 以及最佳模型名称均无法确定。\n\n核查情况：\n- 两次检索（已达每次问答的检索上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。\n- 该文为实验表征类研究，内容涉及纤维形态与打浆度/WRV [1]、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸 [5]、FT-IR 氢键解析 [3]，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度、按 GBT 12914-2008 测湿纸幅强度、按 ISO 15361 测零距抗张强度 [2]。其中没有机器学习或统计预测模型的训练过程、验证集划分，也没有模型间的比较与“最佳模型”的选择。\n- 该文中出现的 R²（如软木纤维各磨浆转数下为 0.9995–0.9996）是 FT-IR 羟基谱带非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非预测模型验证集上的 R²，二者不可混用。\n- 该文结论部分讨论的是 PFI 磨浆过程中超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）的变化，以及 CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量之间的正相关（该相关仅在所研究的软木与硬木浆、0–16,000 转 PFI 磨浆条件下成立，属相关性而非因果，原文亦仅以“might be generally speculated”表述推测）[11][12]。这些都不是预测模型结果。\n\n建议：请提供该论文的标题/DOI 或上传原文 PDF；若您指的是另一篇专门做抗张强度机器学习预测的工作，请告知文献信息，我可再核对其验证集指标与最佳模型名称。",

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28]. Thus, according to the crystallite sizes (as Table 1 shows) and the unit cell parameters of cellulose Iβ, there was most likely to be an average of two-fibrils with an arrangement of 234,432 packed side-by-side for both softwood fibers and hardwood fibers (as seen in Figure 5, drawn with mercury\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. The result is consistent with the report of Haigler & Roberts [26], which shows that there might be two microfibrils associated along part of their length.\n\n[原文片段不连续]\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3.               "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure."
            }

          "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general. It is assumed that PFI refining is an excellent mechanical treatment of fibrillation with relatively little destruction on the supramolecular structure."

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Conclusions\n[原文]\nupramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.PFI refining acts not only on the macro-level structure and mechanical properties, but also on The results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of thethe supramolecular structure, including crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds.",
        "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 4. Conclusions\n[原文]\nThe results indicated that the fibrillation and properties of fibers are related to the variation of the supramolecular structure during PFI refining. It is noticeable that there was a significantly positive correlation between the CI-XI and content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds during PFI refining for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers. Thus, the trend of the content of O(6)H· · · O(3)’ H-bonds might be generally speculated based on CI-XI while refining. Besides, the crystallite size, crystallinity, and content of various H-bonds did not change much in general.         "text": "核查情况：\n- 两次检索（已达每次问答的检索上限）均只命中同一篇文献：Li (2020) 关于 PFI 磨浆对纤维素聚集结构与性能影响的研究 [1][2][7]。\n- 该文为实验表征类研究，内容涉及纤维形态与打浆度/WRV [1]、XRD 结晶度与微晶尺寸 [5]、FT-IR 氢键解析 [3]，以及按 TAPPI T494 实测干纸页抗张强度、按 GBT 12914-2008 测湿纸幅强度、按 ISO 15361 测零距抗张强度 [2]。其中没有机器学习或统计预测模型的训练过程、验证集划分，也没有模型间的比较与“最佳模型”的选择。\n- 该文中出现的 R²（如软木纤维各磨浆转数下为 0.9995–0.9996）是 FT-IR 羟基谱带非线性拟合的拟合优度 [3]，并非预测模型验证集上的 R²，二者不可混用。\n- 该文结论部分讨论的是 PFI 磨浆过程中超分子结构（微晶尺寸、结晶度、各类氢键含量）的变化，以及 CI-XI 与 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量之间的正相关（该相关仅在所研究的软木与硬木浆、0–16,000 转 PFI 磨浆条件下成立，属相关性而非因果，原文亦仅以“might be generally speculated”表述推测）[11][12]。这些都不是预测模型结果。",

PFI2-031 PFI打浆把纤维素从I型变成II型以后，结晶度为什么还会下降？

两版均完成复核并保留否定I→II前提，但都继续扩写无依据II型机制、峰位和测量推断。旧版把相对降幅与百分点比较而误称矛盾；新版仍称线性降幅。Jev两版均无有效评分，Codex补评。

固定初稿
## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）

现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并没有把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）的 XRD 结果显示，两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iα/Iβ 的晶面（如 (1-10)、(110)、(200)）[5]。同一文献也指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾，有的报道下降、有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。

因此在讨论"为什么转变后结晶度还降"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是**峰位**（纤维素 II 的特征峰约在 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°）真的出现，还是仅峰形/峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。

## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能原因

1. **转变过程本身就伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"，后段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶（cocrystallization）并存[6][18]。也就是说：残余晶体可能已重排为 II 型，但同时有相当部分链区被转化为无定形，总量/有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度自然下降。文献中软木 CI‑XI 从 73.23% 降至 69.82%、CI‑XA 从 40.46% 降至 34.20%（16000 转），硬木分别从 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。

2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排带来应变与缺陷。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致——垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒在堆垛方式改变时，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时"下降"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷，而不只是晶型种类。

3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较——所以"结晶度下降"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或 Rietveld 全谱拟合重新验证。

4. **可能的相关机制（本库无证据，属缺口）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I。这一点**未能在本次检索到的文献中找到支撑**（文献库仅有 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不作定量断言。

## 建议的最小验证集
- XRD 报告**原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认是否有 12°/20° 的 II 型峰；
- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 及 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明所用公式的晶型适用性[5]；
- 用 FT-IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 交叉验证晶型与有序度——本文亦用 FT‑IR 氢键解卷积并与 CI 做相关（Pearson r ≈ 0.89–0.91，p<0.05）[3][4]，说明结晶度变化与分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量同向变化，可作为独立判据。

**证据缺口**：关于"纤维素 II 本征结晶度低于纤维素 I"以及"PFI 打浆可诱导 I→II"这两点，本次两轮检索均未获得文献证据；上述第 1–3 条机制有[5][6][12][13][18]支持，第 4 条仅为待验证假设。
旧复核
## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）

现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转），XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）始终未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iβ 的晶面（(110)、(1-10)、(200)）[5]。同一文献指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道结晶度下降，有的报道先升后降或反复波动，尚未有明确一致趋势[1]。

因此在讨论"为什么晶型转变后结晶度还下降"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是否真的出现了纤维素 II 的特征峰（约 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°；这些峰位为一般背景知识，非本文引用），还是仅仅峰形或峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。

## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍可能下降的解释

1. **晶区破坏与残余晶体重排可以并存。** 该文献对 PFI 打浆中结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降表明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"；随后上升可能源于机械与热作用下干燥时无定形区的共结晶（cocrystallization）；末段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。文献还指出，水分子更易从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 晶面渗入准晶区（paracrystalline region），使这些晶面承受更多机械作用，造成链断裂，并在干燥时发生链合并/共结晶；而 (200) 面因水分子难以渗入，裂解作用较弱，其垂直晶粒尺寸反而上升[6][18]。由此可推测：一部分链区可能已重排为另一种堆垛方式，同时另有相当部分链区被转化为无定形区或缺陷区，使整体有序度下降；这是本文机理框架下的一种推测性解释，文中并未讨论 I→II 转变。

   文中报道的数值（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%[12]；硬木 CI‑XI 75.55%→73.55%、CI‑XA 47.16%→38.01%[12]。文中另述的降幅为：软木 CI‑XI 降 4.66%、CI‑XA 降 15.47%；硬木 CI‑XI 降 2.65%、CI‑XA 降 19.4%[8]。注意：硬木 CI‑XI 的绝对降幅按表计算约 2.0 个百分点，与引述的 2.65% 不完全吻合，原文数据存在不一致，引用时应以表中数值为准并说明。

2. **晶粒极小，与"缺陷/应变"难以分离。** 这些浆的晶粒尺寸仅约 3–5 nm（表 1 中 2.9–4.8 nm）[12]，且不同晶面响应不同：垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大，垂直 (200) 面的尺寸则小幅上升[6][12][18]。如此小的晶粒若发生堆垛方式改变，峰宽化与微应变增加会同时拉低面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸——Scherrer 计算未校正仪器展宽，所得尺寸一般低于真实值[5]。因此，这种下降反映的是有序度/缺陷状态，而不只是"晶型种类"。

3. **测量可比性问题（重要不确定性）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 依据纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 附近的无定形最低点计算[5]，属于为纤维素 I 标定的强度比值型指标；CI‑XA 则为结晶峰面积占全谱面积的百分比（Pearson VII 分峰）[5]。两种指标数值差异很大（未打浆软木 73.23% vs 40.46%），作者归因于无定形贡献的过拟合[2][9][12]；二者虽显著相关（软木 r = 0.919，硬木 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）[2][10]，但这只说明同一批 I 型样品内趋势一致，不能证明跨晶型可比。晶型变为 II 后主峰位置改变，用 I 型公式算出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减，因此"结晶度下降"可能部分是指标伪影。需用分峰法[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。

4. **文献缺口（不作断言）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I——这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据**（文献库仅含 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变）。"PFI 打浆本身能否诱导 I→II"同样缺乏文献支持。此外，本回答未查看任何图像像素，涉及峰位与晶面取向的描述均来自正文/表格文字[5][6][12][18]。

## 建议的最小验证集
- 报告 XRD **原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认 12°/20° 附近是否出现 II 型峰；
- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 与 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明公式源自纤维素 Iβ[5]，以及仪器展宽未校正带来的低估[5]；
- 用 FT‑IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 独立验证晶型与有序度；本文另用 FT‑IR 羟基区解卷积与 CI 做相关（Pearson r = 0.888/0.889，p < 0.05）[3][4]，可作为有序度变化的辅助判据。

**证据缺口总结**：第 1–3 条机制分别有[5][6][12][13][18]、[5][6][12][18]、[2][5][9][10][12]支持，但均源自纤维素 I 型样品的 PFI 研究，外推到 I→II 转变属推测；第 4 条为未解决缺口。
新复核
## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）

本次检索到的文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**。Li 等对软木浆和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）后，XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；该文的 XRD 解析也只涉及纤维素 Iα/Iβ 晶面，如 (1-10)、(110)、(200) [5]。同一文献还指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道下降，有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。

因此，在讨论"转变后结晶度为什么还降"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是**峰位**（纤维素 II 的特征峰约在 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°）真的出现，还是仅峰形/峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。本次证据不支持"PFI 打浆诱导 I→II 转变"这一前提。

## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能解释（基于证据的机制，外推部分须验证）

1. **转变过程本身可能伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"，后段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。作者还指出，水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶并存[6][18]。据此可设想：残余晶体虽已重排为 II 型，但相当部分链区被转化为无定形，有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度随之下降。不过，这属于从纤维素 I 体系的外推，作者并未研究纤维素 II 体系。

   实测数据（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%；硬木 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。注意，这些数值对应的是**晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品**，作者同时报告 CI 趋势为"先降后升再降"的波动，而非单调下降[13]。

2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排可能带来应变与缺陷（外推）。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致：垂直 (1-10) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒，若堆垛方式改变，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时"下降"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷变化，而不只是晶型种类。该推论在纤维素 I 数据上成立，向纤维素 II 的外推未经检验。

3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 该文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较，因此"结晶度下降"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。

4. **关于纤维素 II 本征结晶度（证据缺口）**：纤维素 II 由反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸可能低于纤维素 I。但这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据支撑**（库内仅 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不能据此作定量断言。

## 建议的最小验证集
- XRD 报告**原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认是否有 12°/20° 的 II 型峰；
- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 及 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明所用公式的晶型适用性[5]；

 ## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）
 
-现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并没有把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）的 XRD 结果显示，两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iα/Iβ 的晶面（如 (1-10)、(110)、(200)）[5]。同一文献也指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾，有的报道下降、有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。
+现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转），XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）始终未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iβ 的晶面（(110)、(1-10)、(200)）[5]。同一文献指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道结晶度下降，有的报道先升后降或反复波动，尚未有明确一致趋势[1]。

-## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能原因
+## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍可能下降的解释
 
-1. **转变过程本身就伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"，后段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶（cocrystallization）并存[6][18]。也就是说：残余晶体可能已重排为 II 型，但同时有相当部分链区被转化为无定形，总量/有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度自然下降。文献中软木 CI‑XI 从 73.23% 降至 69.82%、CI‑XA 从 40.46% 降至 34.20%（16000 转），硬木分别从 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。
+1. **晶区破坏与残余晶体重排可以并存。** 该文献对 PFI 打浆中结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降表明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"；随后上升可能源于机械与热作用下干燥时无定形区的共结晶（cocrystallization）；末段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。文献还指出，水分子更易从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 晶面渗入准晶区（paracrystalline region），使这些晶面承受更多机械作用，造成链断裂，并在干燥时发生链合并/共结晶；而 (200) 面因水分子难以渗入，裂解作用较弱，其垂直晶粒尺寸反而上升[6][18]。由此可推测：一部分链区可能已重排为另一种堆垛方式，同时另有相当部分链区被转化为无定形区或缺陷区，使整体有序度下降；这是本文机理框架下的一种推测性解释，文中并未讨论 I→II 转变。
 
-2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排带来应变与缺陷。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致——垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒在堆垛方式改变时，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时"下降"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷，而不只是晶型种类。
+   文中报道的数值（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%[12]；硬木 CI‑XI 75.55%→73.55%、CI‑XA 47.16%→38.01%[12]。文中另述的降幅为：软木 CI‑XI 降 4.66%、CI‑XA 降 15.47%；硬木 CI‑XI 降 2.65%、CI‑XA 降 19.4%[8]。注意：硬木 CI‑XI 的绝对降幅按表计算约 2.0 个百分点，与引述的 2.65% 不完全吻合，原文数据存在不一致，引用时应以表中数值为准并说明。
 
-3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较——所以"结晶度下降"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或 Rietveld 全谱拟合重新验证。
+2. **晶粒极小，与"缺陷/应变"难以分离。** 这些浆的晶粒尺寸仅约 3–5 nm（表 1 中 2.9–4.8 nm）[12]，且不同晶面响应不同：垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大，垂直 (200) 面的尺寸则小幅上升[6][12][18]。如此小的晶粒若发生堆垛方式改变，峰宽化与微应变增加会同时拉低面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸——Scherrer 计算未校正仪器展宽，所得尺寸一般低于真实值[5]。因此，这种下降反映的是有序度/缺陷状态，而不只是"晶型种类"。
 
-4. **可能的相关机制（本库无证据，属缺口）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I。这一点**未能在本次检索到的文献中找到支撑**（文献库仅有 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不作定量断言。
+3. **测量可比性问题（重要不确定性）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 依据纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 附近的无定形最低点计算[5]，属于为纤维素 I 标定的强度比值型指标；CI‑XA 则为结晶峰面积占全谱面积的百分比（Pearson VII 分峰）[5]。两种指标数值差异很大（未打浆软木 73.23% vs 40.46%），作者归因于无定形贡献的过拟合[2][9][12]；二者虽显著相关（软木 r = 0.919，硬木 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）[2][10]，但这只说明同一批 I 型样品内趋势一致，不能证明跨晶型可比。晶型变为 II 后主峰位置改变，用 I 型公式算出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减，因此"结晶度下降"可能部分是指标伪影。需用分峰法[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。
+
+4. **文献缺口（不作断言）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I——这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据**（文献库仅含 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变）。"PFI 打浆本身能否诱导 I→II"同样缺乏文献支持。此外，本回答未查看任何图像像素，涉及峰位与晶面取向的描述均来自正文/表格文字[5][6][12][18]。
 
 ## 建议的最小验证集
-- XRD 报告**原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认是否有 12°/20° 的 II 型峰；
-- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 及 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明所用公式的晶型适用性[5]；
-- 用 FT-IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 交叉验证晶型与有序度——本文亦用 FT‑IR 氢键解卷积并与 CI 做相关（Pearson r ≈ 0.89–0.91，p<0.05）[3][4]，说明结晶度变化与分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量同向变化，可作为独立判据。
+- 报告 XRD **原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认 12°/20° 附近是否出现 II 型峰；
+- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 与 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明公式源自纤维素 Iβ[5]，以及仪器展宽未校正带来的低估[5]；
+- 用 FT‑IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 独立验证晶型与有序度；本文另用 FT‑IR 羟基区解卷积与 CI 做相关（Pearson r = 0.888/0.889，p < 0.05）[3][4]，可作为有序度变化的辅助判据。
 
-**证据缺口**：关于"纤维素 II 本征结晶度低于纤维素 I"以及"PFI 打浆可诱导 I→II"这两点，本次两轮检索均未获得文献证据；上述第 1–3 条机制有[5][6][12][13][18]支持，第 4 条仅为待验证假设。
+**证据缺口总结**：第 1–3 条机制分别有[5][6][12][13][18]、[5][6][12][18]、[2][5][9][10][12]支持，但均源自纤维素 I 型样品的 PFI 研究，外推到 I→II 转变属推测；第 4 条为未解决缺口。

    "answer": "## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）\n\n现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转），XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）始终未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于\"相对温和的机械处理\"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iβ 的晶面（(110)、(1-10)、(200)）[5]。同一文献指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道结晶度下降，有的报道先升后降或反复波动，尚未有明确一致趋势[1]。\n\n因此在讨论\"为什么晶型转变后结晶度还下降\"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是否真的出现了纤维素 II 的特征峰（约 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°；这些峰位为一般背景知识，非本文引用），还是仅仅峰形或峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。\n\n## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍可能下降的解释\n\n1. **晶区破坏与残余晶体重排可以并存。** 该文献对 PFI 打浆中结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降表明机械作用\"主要作用于结晶区\"；随后上升可能源于机械与热作用下干燥时无定形区的共结晶（cocrystallization）；末段下降则归因于\"结晶区的持续破坏\"[13]。文献还指出，水分子更易从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 晶面渗入准晶区（paracrystalline region），使这些晶面承受更多机械作用，造成链断裂，并在干燥时发生链合并/共结晶；而 (200) 面因水分子难以渗入，裂解作用较弱，其垂直晶粒尺寸反而上升[6][18]。由此可推测：一部分链区可能已重排为另一种堆垛方式，同时另有相当部分链区被转化为无定形区或缺陷区，使整体有序度下降；这是本文机理框架下的一种推测性解释，文中并未讨论 I→II 转变。\n\n   文中报道的数值（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%[12]；硬木 CI‑XI 75.55%→73.55%、CI‑XA 47.16%→38.01%[12]。文中另述的降幅为：软木 CI‑XI 降 4.66%、CI‑XA 降 15.47%；硬木 CI‑XI 降 2.65%、CI‑XA 降 19.4%[8]。注意：硬木 CI‑XI 的绝对降幅按表计算约 2.0 个百分点，与引述的 2.65% 不完全吻合，原文数据存在不一致，引用时应以表中数值为准并说明。\n\n2. **晶粒极小，与\"缺陷/应变\"难以分离。** 这些浆的晶粒尺寸仅约 3–5 nm（表 1 中 2.9–4.8 nm）[12]，且不同晶面响应不同：垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大，垂直 (200) 面的尺寸则小幅上升[6][12][18]。如此小的晶粒若发生堆垛方式改变，峰宽化与微应变增加会同时拉低面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸——Scherrer 计算未校正仪器展宽，所得尺寸一般低于真实值[5]。因此，这种下降反映的是有序度/缺陷状态，而不只是\"晶型种类\"。\n\n3. **测量可比性问题（重要不确定性）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 依据纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 附近的无定形最低点计算[5]，属于为纤维素 I 标定的强度比值型指标；CI‑XA 则为结晶峰面积占全谱面积的百分比（Pearson VII 分峰）[5]。两种指标数值差异很大（未打浆软木 73.23% vs 40.46%），作者归因于无定形贡献的过拟合[2][9][12]；二者虽显著相关（软木 r = 0.919，硬木 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）[2][10]，但这只说明同一批 I 型样品内趋势一致，不能证明跨晶型可比。晶型变为 II 后主峰位置改变，用 I 型公式算出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减，因此\"结晶度下降\"可能部分是指标伪影。需用分峰法[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。\n\n4. **文献缺口（不作断言）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I——这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据**（文献库仅含 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变）。\"PFI 打浆本身能否诱导 I→II\"同样缺乏文献支持。此外，本回答未查看任何图像像素，涉及峰位与晶面取向的描述均来自正文/表格文字[5][6][12][18]。\n\n## 建议的最小验证集\n- 报告 XRD **原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认 12°/20° 附近是否出现 II 型峰；\n- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 与 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明公式源自纤维素 Iβ[5]，以及仪器展宽未校正带来的低估[5]；\n- 用 FT‑IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 独立验证晶型与有序度；本文另用 FT‑IR 羟基区解卷积与 CI 做相关（Pearson r = 0.888/0.889，p < 0.05）[3][4]，可作为有序度变化的辅助判据。\n\n**证据缺口总结**：第 1–3 条机制分别有[5][6][12][13][18]、[5][6][12][18]、[2][5][9][10][12]支持，但均源自纤维素 I 型样品的 PFI 研究，外推到 I→II 转变属推测；第 4 条为未解决缺口。",

        "ref": "[1]",
        "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

          "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds."

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2.         "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. Frequently adopted arrangements of the 18 cellulose chains are 234432, 34443, and 333333 [27]. Therein, 234432 arrangement was found to be more probable based on calculation [28].         "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 未确定\n[原文]\nAbstract: Supramolecular structure is the critical factor that afects the properties of cellulosic fibers. This article studied the action of Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining on the molecular aggregation and hydrogen bonding network, and tried to explore the relationship between the crystal packing and hydrogen-bonding network in cellulosic fibers. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. Therein, the content of the inter-molecular O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) H-bonds was significantly correlated with the crystalline index that was obtained in intensities of the XRD peaks. The Pearson correlation coeficient between them was 0.888 (p < 0.05) for softwood fibers and 0.889 (p < 0.05) for hardwood fibers, respectively. It can be concluded that the variations of accessibility, swelling, and fibrillation were closely related to the supramolecular structure and the intermolecular H-bonds play an important role in the crystal packing of cellulose.",

        "id": "C1",
        "text": "## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）\n\n现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转），XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）始终未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于\"相对温和的机械处理\"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iβ 的晶面（(110)、(1-10)、(200)）[5]。同一文献指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道结晶度下降，有的报道先升后降或反复波动，尚未有明确一致趋势[1]。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "E24",
        "basis": {
          "type": "reference_evidence",
          "text": "The cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show."
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "C2",
        "text": "因此在讨论\"为什么晶型转变后结晶度还下降\"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是否真的出现了纤维素 II 的特征峰（约 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°；这些峰位为一般背景知识，非本文引用），还是仅仅峰形或峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "unsupported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C3",
        "text": "## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍可能下降的解释\n\n1. **晶区破坏与残余晶体重排可以并存。** 该文献对 PFI 打浆中结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降表明机械作用\"主要作用于结晶区\"；随后上升可能源于机械与热作用下干燥时无定形区的共结晶（cocrystallization）；末段下降则归因于\"结晶区的持续破坏\"[13]。文献还指出，水分子更易从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 晶面渗入准晶区（paracrystalline region），使这些晶面承受更多机械作用，造成链断裂，并在干燥时发生链合并/共结晶；而 (200) 面因水分子难以渗入，裂解作用较弱，其垂直晶粒尺寸反而上升[6][18]。由此可推测：一部分链区可能已重排为另一种堆垛方式，同时另有相当部分链区被转化为无定形区或缺陷区，使整体有序度下降；这是本文机理框架下的一种推测性解释，文中并未讨论 I→II 转变。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C4",
        "text": "文中报道的数值（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%[12]；硬木 CI‑XI 75.55%→73.55%、CI‑XA 47.16%→38.01%[12]。文中另述的降幅为：软木 CI‑XI 降 4.66%、CI‑XA 降 15.47%；硬木 CI‑XI 降 2.65%、CI‑XA 降 19.4%[8]。注意：硬木 CI‑XI 的绝对降幅按表计算约 2.0 个百分点，与引述的 2.65% 不完全吻合，原文数据存在不一致，引用时应以表中数值为准并说明。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C5",
        "text": "2. **晶粒极小，与\"缺陷/应变\"难以分离。** 这些浆的晶粒尺寸仅约 3–5 nm（表 1 中 2.9–4.8 nm）[12]，且不同晶面响应不同：垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大，垂直 (200) 面的尺寸则小幅上升[6][12][18]。如此小的晶粒若发生堆垛方式改变，峰宽化与微应变增加会同时拉低面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸——Scherrer 计算未校正仪器展宽，所得尺寸一般低于真实值[5]。因此，这种下降反映的是有序度/缺陷状态，而不只是\"晶型种类\"。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C6",
        "text": "3. **测量可比性问题（重要不确定性）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 依据纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 附近的无定形最低点计算[5]，属于为纤维素 I 标定的强度比值型指标；CI‑XA 则为结晶峰面积占全谱面积的百分比（Pearson VII 分峰）[5]。两种指标数值差异很大（未打浆软木 73.23% vs 40.46%），作者归因于无定形贡献的过拟合[2][9][12]；二者虽显著相关（软木 r = 0.919，硬木 r = 0.925，p < 0.05）[2][10]，但这只说明同一批 I 型样品内趋势一致，不能证明跨晶型可比。晶型变为 II 后主峰位置改变，用 I 型公式算出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减，因此\"结晶度下降\"可能部分是指标伪影。需用分峰法[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C7",
        "text": "4. **文献缺口（不作断言）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I——这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据**（文献库仅含 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变）。\"PFI 打浆本身能否诱导 I→II\"同样缺乏文献支持。此外，本回答未查看任何图像像素，涉及峰位与晶面取向的描述均来自正文/表格文字[5][6][12][18]。",

      {
        "id": "C8",
        "text": "## 建议的最小验证集\n- 报告 XRD **原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认 12°/20° 附近是否出现 II 型峰；\n- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 与 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明公式源自纤维素 Iβ[5]，以及仪器展宽未校正带来的低估[5]；\n- 用 FT‑IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 独立验证晶型与有序度；本文另用 FT‑IR 羟基区解卷积与 CI 做相关（Pearson r = 0.888/0.889，p < 0.05）[3][4]，可作为有序度变化的辅助判据。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C9",
        "text": "**证据缺口总结**：第 1–3 条机制分别有[5][6][12][13][18]、[5][6][12][18]、[2][5][9][10][12]支持，但均源自纤维素 I 型样品的 PFI 研究，外推到 I→II 转变属推测；第 4 条为未解决缺口。",
        "claim_type": "scope",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      }
    ],

 ## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）
 
-现有文献中，PFI 打浆**并没有把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**：Li 等对软木和硬木浆 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）的 XRD 结果显示，两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；其 XRD 解析也只考虑纤维素 Iα/Iβ 的晶面（如 (1-10)、(110)、(200)）[5]。同一文献也指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾，有的报道下降、有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。
+本次检索到的文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**。Li 等对软木浆和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）后，XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于"相对温和的机械处理"[3]；该文的 XRD 解析也只涉及纤维素 Iα/Iβ 晶面，如 (1-10)、(110)、(200) [5]。同一文献还指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道下降，有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。
 
-因此在讨论"为什么转变后结晶度还降"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是**峰位**（纤维素 II 的特征峰约在 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°）真的出现，还是仅峰形/峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。
+因此，在讨论"转变后结晶度为什么还降"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是**峰位**（纤维素 II 的特征峰约在 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°）真的出现，还是仅峰形/峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。本次证据不支持"PFI 打浆诱导 I→II 转变"这一前提。
 
-## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能原因
+## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能解释（基于证据的机制，外推部分须验证）
 
-1. **转变过程本身就伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"，后段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶（cocrystallization）并存[6][18]。也就是说：残余晶体可能已重排为 II 型，但同时有相当部分链区被转化为无定形，总量/有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度自然下降。文献中软木 CI‑XI 从 73.23% 降至 69.82%、CI‑XA 从 40.46% 降至 34.20%（16000 转），硬木分别从 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。
+1. **转变过程本身可能伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用"主要作用于结晶区"，后段下降则归因于"结晶区的持续破坏"[13]。作者还指出，水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶并存[6][18]。据此可设想：残余晶体虽已重排为 II 型，但相当部分链区被转化为无定形，有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度随之下降。不过，这属于从纤维素 I 体系的外推，作者并未研究纤维素 II 体系。
 
-2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排带来应变与缺陷。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致——垂直 (110) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒在堆垛方式改变时，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时"下降"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷，而不只是晶型种类。
+   实测数据（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%；硬木 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。注意，这些数值对应的是**晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品**，作者同时报告 CI 趋势为"先降后升再降"的波动，而非单调下降[13]。
 
-3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 本文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较——所以"结晶度下降"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或 Rietveld 全谱拟合重新验证。
+2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排可能带来应变与缺陷（外推）。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致：垂直 (1-10) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒，若堆垛方式改变，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时"下降"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷变化，而不只是晶型种类。该推论在纤维素 I 数据上成立，向纤维素 II 的外推未经检验。
 
-4. **可能的相关机制（本库无证据，属缺口）**：纤维素 II 反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸通常低于纤维素 I。这一点**未能在本次检索到的文献中找到支撑**（文献库仅有 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不作定量断言。
+3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 该文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较，因此"结晶度下降"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。
+
+4. **关于纤维素 II 本征结晶度（证据缺口）**：纤维素 II 由反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸可能低于纤维素 I。但这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据支撑**（库内仅 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不能据此作定量断言。
 
 ## 建议的最小验证集
 - XRD 报告**原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认是否有 12°/20° 的 II 型峰；
 - 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 及 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明所用公式的晶型适用性[5]；
-- 用 FT-IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 交叉验证晶型与有序度——本文亦用 FT‑IR 氢键解卷积并与 CI 做相关（Pearson r ≈ 0.89–0.91，p<0.05）[3][4]，说明结晶度变化与分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量同向变化，可作为独立判据。
+- 用 FT-IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 交叉验证晶型与有序度。本文用 FT‑IR 氢键解卷积与 CI 做相关分析，Pearson r ≈ 0.89–0.91（p<0.05），说明结晶度变化与分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量同向变化[3][4]；这是相关性，不代表因果，可作为独立判据的辅助。
 
-**证据缺口**：关于"纤维素 II 本征结晶度低于纤维素 I"以及"PFI 打浆可诱导 I→II"这两点，本次两轮检索均未获得文献证据；上述第 1–3 条机制有[5][6][12][13][18]支持，第 4 条仅为待验证假设。
+**证据缺口**：关于"纤维素 II 本征结晶度低于纤维素 I"以及"PFI 打浆可诱导 I→II"这两点，本次两轮检索均未获得文献证据；上述第 1–3 条机制有[5][6][12][13][18]支持（但均在晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品上得出），第 4 条为未验证假设。

    "answer": "## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）\n\n本次检索到的文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**。Li 等对软木浆和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）后，XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于\"相对温和的机械处理\"[3]；该文的 XRD 解析也只涉及纤维素 Iα/Iβ 晶面，如 (1-10)、(110)、(200) [5]。同一文献还指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道下降，有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。\n\n因此，在讨论\"转变后结晶度为什么还降\"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是**峰位**（纤维素 II 的特征峰约在 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°）真的出现，还是仅峰形/峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。本次证据不支持\"PFI 打浆诱导 I→II 转变\"这一前提。\n\n## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能解释（基于证据的机制，外推部分须验证）\n\n1. **转变过程本身可能伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用\"主要作用于结晶区\"，后段下降则归因于\"结晶区的持续破坏\"[13]。作者还指出，水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶并存[6][18]。据此可设想：残余晶体虽已重排为 II 型，但相当部分链区被转化为无定形，有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度随之下降。不过，这属于从纤维素 I 体系的外推，作者并未研究纤维素 II 体系。\n\n   实测数据（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%；硬木 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。注意，这些数值对应的是**晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品**，作者同时报告 CI 趋势为\"先降后升再降\"的波动，而非单调下降[13]。\n\n2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排可能带来应变与缺陷（外推）。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致：垂直 (1-10) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒，若堆垛方式改变，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时\"下降\"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷变化，而不只是晶型种类。该推论在纤维素 I 数据上成立，向纤维素 II 的外推未经检验。\n\n3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 该文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较，因此\"结晶度下降\"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。\n\n4. **关于纤维素 II 本征结晶度（证据缺口）**：纤维素 II 由反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸可能低于纤维素 I。但这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据支撑**（库内仅 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不能据此作定量断言。\n\n## 建议的最小验证集\n- XRD 报告**原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认是否有 12°/20° 的 II 型峰；\n- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 及 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明所用公式的晶型适用性[5]；\n- 用 FT-IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 交叉验证晶型与有序度。本文用 FT‑IR 氢键解卷积与 CI 做相关分析，Pearson r ≈ 0.89–0.91（p<0.05），说明结晶度变化与分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量同向变化[3][4]；这是相关性，不代表因果，可作为独立判据的辅助。\n\n**证据缺口**：关于\"纤维素 II 本征结晶度低于纤维素 I\"以及\"PFI 打浆可诱导 I→II\"这两点，本次两轮检索均未获得文献证据；上述第 1–3 条机制有[5][6][12][13][18]支持（但均在晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品上得出），第 4 条为未验证假设。",

        "ref": "[1]",
        "text": "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds."

Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nRecently, researches indicated that plant cell walls commonly contained microfibrils with 18 cellulose chains [26]. It is well known that two polymorphs, cellulose Iα and Iβ, are present in native cellulose; for clarity, all of the reflections indexed here are on the Iβ lattice. Before analysis, the experimental data is nine point smoothed with Savitzky–Golay algorithm. Results and Discussions > 3.2. Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. The fluctuation of the CI was probably because of the mechanical action of PFI refining on the diferent regions of cellulose. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 3. Results and Discussions > 3.2.         "[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nMechanical, chemical, and biological treatments are usually adopted to obtain the desired physical and mechanical properties and for further utilization of the natural cellulosic fibers. Therein, Papirindustriens forskningsinstitut (PFI) refining is the most common laboratory refiner in order to improve the inter-fiber bonding capacity [1] and accessibility [2,3], and manufacture the micro-fibrillated or nano-fibrillated cellulose [4–6]. The main efects of PFI refining on fibers are: (i) internal fibrillation—delaminating, loosening, and swelling of fiber wall; (ii) external fibrillation—peeling of fibrils from the fiber surface while remaining attached; (iii) fiber shortening—fiber cutting due to shearing action, and (iv) fines formation—primary fines come from ray cells and parenchyma cells and microfibrils that are caused by fiber shortening or external fibrillation. Moreover, the PFI refining could be adopted to obtain a higher internal fibrillation than other laboratory refiners [1]. These efects of the PFI refining on cellulosic fibers will improve the accessibility, the swelling, the flexibility, and the inter-fiber bonding capacity of fibers.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\n It is assumed that these changes in the macro-level structure and properties are related to the changes of crystallinity and H-bonding network during refining [7,8].\n\nThere are some diferent conclusions regarding to the efects of PFI refining on crystallinity of cellulose, not like that of ball milling, which efectively reduces the crystallinity as the treatment progresses. Although some researchers considered that the crystallinity decreased during PFI refining for corn stover [9] or softwood pulp [10], some researchers reported that the crystallinity increased first and then decreased with the degree of refining for hardwood bleached kraft pulp fibers [11] or for unbleached eucalyptus fibers [12]. Moreover, Zhao et al. [7] reported that the crystallinity initially fluctuated upward and then downward, followed by a repeating fluctuation with PFI refining for tobacco stem mechanical pulp. None of the previous studies identified a clear trend, but the results were that the crystallinity varied during PFI refinement. Based on the large proportion of H-bonds in crystalline region of cellulose, it can be assumed that the H-bonding network might change during PFI refining.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nFourier transformation infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), which is sensitive to molecular structure, can be as an indirect measurement for studying H-bonding network. FT-IR deconvolution of hydroxyl groups band was adopted in order to study the changes of the energy of H-bonds and the H-bonding distance during delignification [13] or the deconstruction of cellulose [14]. Moreover, it was used to study the diferences of the content of H-bonds not only between dislocation region and normal region [15], but also among plant species [16,17]. Regarding the changes of H-bonding network during PFI refining, Yuan et al. [18] reported that the content of H-bonds and crystallinity index (CI) of eucalyptus fibers changed with the increment of beating time. Subsequently, Zhao et al. [8] found that the H-bonding energy for O(6)H· · · O(3<sup>0</sup>) inter-molecular H-bonds decreased by 12.9% and evolutions of the content of certain H-bonds difered at various refining stages.\n\n[章节标签（程序整理，非原文）] 1. Introduction\n[原文]\nThere is still a lack of literature on the efects of PFI refinement on the H-bonding network. Particularly, the relationship between the content of H-bonds and crystallinity is still worthy of further study, which will deepen the understanding of the molecular aggregation and distribution of H-bonds, providing a molecular-scale explanation for the variations in accessibility, swelling, flexibility, and fibrillation of cellulosic fibers during PFI refinement. Therefore, this work explored the efects of PFI refinement on the CI, crystallite size, energy of H-bonds, H-bonding distance, and content of H-bonds for softwood pulp fibers and hardwood pulp fibers. Attempts were made in order to establish the correlations between the CI and content of various H-bonds.",

Efect of PFI Refining on Crystalline Index and Crystallite Size\n[原文]\nThe trends of CI (CI-XI and CI-XA) for softwood fibers and hardwood fibers were all similar, decreasing first and then increasing, along with a decline, as shown in Figure 4. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The results showed that the polymorph, H-bonding distance, and H-bonding energy of various H-bonds remained almost unchanged, while the crystalline index, crystallite size, and content of various H-bonds changed with refining. In the first refining stage, the decrease of the CI showed that mechanical treatment may mainly act in the crystalline region. Subsequently, the growth of the CI could be interpreted as greater force acting on the amorphous region in which cocrystallization might occur upon drying under the mechanical and thermal action of PFI refining. The subsequent decrease might be the continuous destruction of crystalline region.",

  "final_codex_review": {
    "key_point_scores": {
      "P1": 1,
      "P2": 1
    },
    "claim_assessments": [
      {
        "id": "C1",
        "text": "## 先核对一个前提（证据与问题设定不完全一致）\n\n本次检索到的文献中，PFI 打浆**并未把纤维素从 I 型变成 II 型**。Li 等对软木浆和硬木浆进行 PFI 打浆（0–16000 转）后，XRD 结果显示两种纤维的**晶型（polymorph）全程未变**，作者据此认为 PFI 属于\"相对温和的机械处理\"[3]；该文的 XRD 解析也只涉及纤维素 Iα/Iβ 晶面，如 (1-10)、(110)、(200) [5]。同一文献还指出，关于 PFI 打浆对结晶度的影响，前人结论互相矛盾：有的报道下降，有的报道先升后降，并无一致趋势[1]。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "supported",
        "basis_locator": "E24",
        "basis": {
          "type": "reference_evidence",
          "text": "The cellulose polymorph of these two fibers had no change during PFI treatment, which illustrates that the PFI refining is a relatively mild mechanical treatment, as the results of XRD in Online Resource (Figures S1 and S2) show."
        }
      },
      {
        "id": "C2",
        "text": "因此，在讨论\"转变后结晶度为什么还降\"之前，建议先确认 XRD 上究竟是**峰位**（纤维素 II 的特征峰约在 2θ ≈ 12°、20°、21.8°）真的出现，还是仅峰形/峰强度变化被解读为晶型转变。本次证据不支持\"PFI 打浆诱导 I→II 转变\"这一前提。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "unsupported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C3",
        "text": "## 若确实发生了 I→II，结晶度仍下降的可能解释（基于证据的机制，外推部分须验证）\n\n1. **转变过程本身可能伴随晶区破坏，两者并不互斥。** 该文献对 PFI 结晶度波动的解释是：初期 CI 下降说明机械作用\"主要作用于结晶区\"，后段下降则归因于\"结晶区的持续破坏\"[13]。作者还指出，水分子优先从亲水的 (1-10)/(110) 面渗入**准晶区（paracrystalline）**，使这些晶面更易受机械作用，造成链断裂与干燥时的共结晶并存[6][18]。据此可设想：残余晶体虽已重排为 II 型，但相当部分链区被转化为无定形，有序尺寸变小，表观结晶度随之下降。不过，这属于从纤维素 I 体系的外推，作者并未研究纤维素 II 体系。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C4",
        "text": "实测数据（16000 转 vs 未打浆）：软木 CI‑XI 73.23%→69.82%、CI‑XA 40.46%→34.20%；硬木 75.55%→73.55%、47.16%→38.01%[12]；线性降幅报道为软木 −4.66%/−15.47%、硬木 −2.65%/−19.4%[8]。注意，这些数值对应的是**晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品**，作者同时报告 CI 趋势为\"先降后升再降\"的波动，而非单调下降[13]。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C5",
        "text": "2. **晶粒尺寸极小，晶型重排可能带来应变与缺陷（外推）。** 这些浆的晶粒垂直方向尺寸仅约 3–5 nm[12]，且不同晶面响应不一致：垂直 (1-10) 面的尺寸波动最大（水化 + 机械作用），而垂直 (200) 面的尺寸反而上升（相邻微纤丝 (200) 面在干燥时对齐、链合并）[6][18]。如此小的晶粒，若堆垛方式改变，峰宽化/应变增加会使面积法结晶度和 Scherrer 晶粒尺寸同时\"下降\"，这反映的是有序度/缺陷变化，而不只是晶型种类。该推论在纤维素 I 数据上成立，向纤维素 II 的外推未经检验。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C6",
        "text": "3. **测量层面的可比性问题（重要）。** 该文的 CI‑XI 用纤维素 Iβ 的 (200) 峰（2θ 22–23°）与 18–19° 的无定形谷计算[5]，这是为纤维素 I 标定的 Segal 类指标；两种指标本身差异巨大（如未打浆软木 CI‑XI 73.23% vs CI‑XA 40.46%，作者归因于无定形贡献过拟合）[2][9][12]。晶型换成 II 后主峰位置改变，同一公式给出的数值不宜与 I 型样品直接相减比较，因此\"结晶度下降\"中可能有一部分是指标伪影，而非真实结晶度变化。相关结论需用分峰法（Pearson VII 等）[5]或全谱拟合重新验证。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C7",
        "text": "4. **关于纤维素 II 本征结晶度（证据缺口）**：纤维素 II 由反平行链堆垛、经溶胀/去晶化路径生成，其本征结晶度与晶粒尺寸可能低于纤维素 I。但这一点在本次检索到的文献中**没有证据支撑**（库内仅 1 篇 PFI 相关文献，且其样品晶型未变），因此不能据此作定量断言。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "unsupported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C8",
        "text": "## 建议的最小验证集\n- XRD 报告**原始峰位与分峰参数**（不只报一个 CI 数），确认是否有 12°/20° 的 II 型峰；\n- 同时给出 CI‑XI、CI‑XA 及 Scherrer 尺寸，并注明所用公式的晶型适用性[5]；\n- 用 FT-IR（如 1430/897 cm⁻¹ 比值）或 CP/MAS ¹³C NMR 交叉验证晶型与有序度。本文用 FT‑IR 氢键解卷积与 CI 做相关分析，Pearson r ≈ 0.89–0.91（p<0.05），说明结晶度变化与分子间 O(6)H···O(3′) 氢键含量同向变化[3][4]；这是相关性，不代表因果，可作为独立判据的辅助。",
        "claim_type": "fact",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      },
      {
        "id": "C9",
        "text": "**证据缺口**：关于\"纤维素 II 本征结晶度低于纤维素 I\"以及\"PFI 打浆可诱导 I→II\"这两点，本次两轮检索均未获得文献证据；上述第 1–3 条机制有[5][6][12][13][18]支持（但均在晶型未变的纤维素 I 样品上得出），第 4 条为未验证假设。",
        "claim_type": "scope",
        "support": "partially_supported",
        "basis_locator": "NONE",
        "basis": null
      }
    ],
